 \frac{(-1)^{(j-1)/2}}{j}\sqrt{\frac{w_n}{w_{n-j}}}\,
 \varphi_{n-j},\qquad \varphi_n=p_n/\sqrt{h_n}.
 \tag{FEX10}
\]
The mass $M_s$ cancels from this ratio, not from the underlying norms.
Let $H_D=\sum_{j=1}^D1/j$ and $H_0=0$. For $n>m\ge1$, $b\ge1/2$ gives
$w_n/w_m\le\sqrt{n/m}$ and $w_n\le2\sqrt n$. Indeed square each factor
$j/(j-1/2)$ and use $j(j-1)\le(j-1/2)^2$; the product telescopes.
Apply the weighted Schur estimate to the absolute matrix in FEX10 with
weights $w_n^{-1/2}$. Its row sum is at most $H_D$; its column sum at $n$
is at most $H_n+4$. The excess for $1\le m<n$ is bounded by
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{n/m}-1}{n-m}
 =\frac1{\sqrt m(\sqrt n+\sqrt m)}\le\frac1{\sqrt{nm}},
\]
whose sum is at most two; the $m=0$ term is at most $2/\sqrt n\le2$.
Enlarging the odd-index sums is legitimate because all terms are
nonnegative. Cauchy--Schwarz in each weighted row and then summing the
column estimate proves
\[
 \|\partial_y\|_{\mathcal P_D}\le\sqrt{H_D(H_D+4)}\le H_D+2,
 \qquad \|f(y+z)\|\le e^{|z|(H_D+2)}\|f\|.
 \tag{FEX11}
\]
At $D=0$ the derivative is zero. Translation is the exact finite Taylor
exponential. The coordinate substitution $S=c_0+iy$ gives
$\partial_S=-i\partial_y$ with the same norm.

Retain every actual coefficient in
\[
 A_*^{\rm abs}=\sum_\nu|a_\nu|,\quad B_*^{\rm sh}=\max_\nu|b_\nu|,
 \quad C_v=\frac{A_*^{\rm abs}(B_*^{\rm sh})^v}{|\mu_v|}\ge1,
 \qquad P_D=C_v e^{B_*^{\rm sh}(H_D+2)}.
 \tag{FEX12}
\]
Since $|\mu_{v+n}|\le A_*^{\rm abs}(B_*^{\rm sh})^{v+n}$ and
$v!/(v+n)!\le1/n!$, the triangle inequality in FEX10--11 gives
\[
 \|B_q(\partial_S)\|_{s,c_0;\mathcal P_D}\le P_D.
 \tag{FEX13}
\]
This bound holds for the literal fixed polynomial $B_q$ on any explicitly
specified finite degree space. On $D\le q-1$ it is the original AIE
operator, whose matrix is triangular with diagonal one. FEX8 therefore
proves its new exterior estimate
\[
\boxed{\quad
 P_D^{-2t}\le
 \frac{\det(X^*(B_q^{-1})^*B_q^{-1}X)}{\det(X^*X)}
 \le \min\{N_{D,s}^{2t},P_D^{2(D+1-t)}\}.
 \quad}\tag{FEX14}
\]
Here $X$ is any original $t$-plane in $\mathcal P_D$ and $N_{D,s}$ is the
unchanged AIE10 inverse bound. The new bound requires neither a new
zero-free disk nor a lower bound on an unevaluated restricted minor.
For $D=q-1$, $t=r$, its upper logarithm is at most
\[
 2(q-r)\{\log C_v+B_*^{\rm sh}(H_{q-1}+2)\}
       =O_{\mathsf H,\delta,\gamma}(q\log q)=o(kq).
 \tag{FEX15}
\]
Thus the factor $rD$ in the old exterior allowance is unnecessary. The
forward norm, together with the full Jacobian, controls the product;
raising the worst inverse singular value to the $r$th power loses that
information.

There is a direct high-source extension of this statement, distinguished
from changing AIE's cutoff. For a fixed $k$ use the same polynomial
$B_q(\partial_S)$ on each $\mathcal P_N$. Map the exact flag
\[
 \chi\mathcal P_{N-q}\ \subset\ I_K\mathbb C^r+\chi\mathcal P_{N-q}
\]
to its literal image under $B_q$. Its relation space is
$B_q(\partial_S)(\chi\mathcal P_{N-q})$, not the original ideal by
assumption. Its whole Jacobian is one, and FEX13 is valid on this newly
specified domain. If $\widetilde F_K$ is the signed kernel determinant
using the native source norm on these transported flags, FEX6 gives
\[
 -2(2q+1)\log P_{2q}\le\widetilde F_K-F_K
              \le2(4q+1)\log P_{2q}.
 \tag{FEX16}
\]
Indeed at endpoint $N$ its logarithmic Gram change belongs to
$[-2(N+1-r)\log P_N,2r\log P_N]$. Insert the four original signs and
use $P_N\le P_{2q}$. This is an exact extension and a signed estimate;
no commutation with the original remainder map has been assumed.

\section{The literal conductor at every source endpoint}
\label{sec:FEX-conductor}
The previous high-source extension is useful, but the actual conductor
provides a more informative reduction. On $\mathcal P_N$, $N\ge q-1$,
its exact Taylor identity is
\[
\begin{gathered}
 \mathcal C_A=\partial_S^v B^{[N]}(\partial_S),\qquad
 B^{[N]}(X)=\sum_{n=0}^{N-v}
       \frac{v!\mu_{v+n}}{(v+n)!\mu_v}X^n,\\
 B^{[q-1]}=B_q,\qquad
 L:=\ker(\mathcal C_A|_{\mathcal P_N})=\mathcal P_{v-1},\quad
 \mathcal C_A:\mathcal P_N/L\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal P_{N-v}.
\end{gathered}\tag{FEX17}
\]
For $v=0$, $L=0$. These assertions follow either from the leading
nonzero derivative or from the commuting invertible triangular factor
$B^{[N]}$. Thus the operator on the high endpoints is defined by the
original translations themselves. It is not obtained by silently
changing the cutoff in the definition of $B_q$.

The domain has its original quotient Gamma norm at centre $c$; the
codomain has its native Gamma norm at centre $c'$. Define
\[
 M_N=\max\left\{1,\frac{v!}{|\mu_v|}
       \sum_\nu|a_\nu|e^{|b_\nu-4|(H_N+2)}\right\},\qquad m_N=\log M_N.
 \tag{FEX18}
\]
The difference of centres is essential: $S'+b_\nu=c+iy+(b_\nu-4)$.
FEX11 proves $\|\mathcal C_Ap\|_{s,c'}\le M_N\|p\|_{s,c}$.
Taking the infimum over the same $L$-coset gives the same bound for the
induced isomorphism in FEX17.

Its squared whole-space Jacobian is explicitly
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \mathscr J_{N,s}
  =\prod_{d=v}^{N}\frac{w_d}{w_{d-v}}
  =\frac{\prod_{d=N-v+1}^{N}w_d}{\prod_{d=0}^{v-1}w_d}.
 \quad}\tag{FEX19}
\]
Products are one when $v=0$. To prove the formula, take the orthonormal
quotient basis represented by $\varphi_v((S-c)/i),\ldots,
\varphi_N((S-c)/i)$, with the normalization in FEX10, and the corresponding
native basis at $c'$. The triangular diagonal of the map is
$i^{-v}(d)_v\sqrt{h_{d-v}/h_d}$, where $(d)_v=d!/(d-v)!$ is a falling
factorial in this formula. Its squared modulus is $w_d/w_{d-v}$.
The source mass is present in both $h$ factors before cancellation;
translation of the centre affects only strictly lower coefficients.
Telescoping proves the second equality, including overlapping product
ranges. For the unnormalized $\mathcal T_A$ the squared Jacobian is
$|\mu_v/v!|^{2(N+1-v)}\mathscr J_{N,s}$.

Put $\zeta_{N,s}=\log\mathscr J_{N,s}$. The following finite bounds
will suffice:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 0\le\zeta_{N,1}\le v\log(2\sqrt N),&s=1,\\[2pt]
 0\le-\zeta_{N,s}\le v(b-1)H_N,&s=k\ge9.
\end{array}\tag{FEX20}
\]
For the first use monotonicity of $w_n$ and $1\le w_n\le2\sqrt n$.
For the second, $w_n$ decreases and
$-\log w_n=\sum_{j=1}^n\log(1+(b-1)/j)\le(b-1)H_n$; then use the second
product formula in FEX19. These proofs also show directly that the
Jacobian error at the tensor source is $O(vk\log q)$, rather than an
uncontrolled determinant of dimension $q$.

The old explicit AIE inverse is still compatible with this estimate.
For example, let $R_A$ be that right inverse for the unnormalized
$\mathcal T_A:\mathcal P_D\to\mathcal P_{D-v}$, and let $R_{\min}$ be
its actual minimum-norm right inverse. Their difference takes values in
$L$ and is orthogonal to $R_{\min}$. On a $t$-plane $X$ in the target,
\[
 \det((R_AX)^*R_AX)
 \le \det((R_{\min}X)^*R_{\min}X)
       (1+M_{\rm raw}^2 C_{A,D,s}^2)^{\min(t,v)}.
 \tag{FEX21}
\]
Here $\|\mathcal T_A\|\le M_{\rm raw}$ and $\|R_A\|\le C_{A,D,s}$
are the original finite forward and AIE22 bounds. Indeed the excess
Gram has rank at most $v$, and $R_{\min}^*R_{\min}\succeq
M_{\rm raw}^{-2}I$. The operator $R_A-R_{\min}$ is an orthogonal
projection of $R_A$, so its norm is at most $C_{A,D,s}$. Apply the
matrix determinant lemma, or congruence with the minimum Gram, to obtain
FEX21. FEX6 bounds the minimum inverse determinant by
$J_{\rm raw}^{-1}M_{\rm raw}^{2(D+1-v-t)}\det(X^*X)$.
Only the fixed rank $v$, not $t$, multiplies the exponential allowance
for the raw low-degree correction. The main reduction below avoids that
raw correction by retaining its exact two quotient metrics instead.

\section{The residual observation and the smaller coefficient space}
\label{sec:FEX-residual}
AKJ12--25 identifies the original conductor preimage as
\[
 V_A=\{p\in\mathcal P_{q-1}:\psi\mid\mathcal T_Ap\}.
 \tag{FEX22}
\]
Its complete degree-adapted basis is $1,S,\ldots,S^{v-1}$ followed by
\[
 P_h=\frac{(q'+h+v)!}{(q'+h)!}
            B_q(\partial_S)^{-1}\mathcal J_v(\psi(S)S^h),
 \quad 0\le h<a-v,
 \qquad \mathcal J_vS^d=\frac{d!}{(d+v)!}S^{d+v}.
 \tag{FEX23}
\]
The variable in this inverse coefficient expression is identified with
$S'$ after applying the translation map. Each $P_h$ is monic of degree
$q'+v+h$. Its normalized conductor image is exactly
\[
 \mathcal C_AP_h=d_h\psi(S')S'^h,
 \qquad d_h=\frac{(q'+h+v)!}{(q'+h)!}.
 \tag{FEX24}
\]
The full original residual matrix in this basis is
$\Xi=(\Xi_{\rm lo},\Xi_{\rm hi})$, of size $j_k$ by $a$ and rank $j_k$.
Its kernel maps isomorphically onto the original $K$. These are the
supplied actual coefficient maps, not independent matrix parameters.
Put
\[
 r_{\rm lo}=\operatorname{rank}\Xi_{\rm lo},\quad
 t_0=v-r_{\rm lo}=\dim(K\cap L),\quad t=r-t_0.
 \tag{FEX25}
\]
Choose a quotient coordinate map $Q_{\rm lo}$ with kernel exactly
$\operatorname{im}\Xi_{\rm lo}$, and a full-column-rank basis $W_k$ of
\[
 \ker(Q_{\rm lo}\Xi_{\rm hi})\subset\mathbb C^{a-v}.
 \tag{FEX26}
\]
The residual map has rank $j_k-r_{\rm lo}$ because the full matrix has
rank $j_k$. Hence the space in FEX26 has dimension $t$. These choices
are made using actual nonzero minors and then kept fixed as the source
endpoint changes. No generic minor or generic rank is substituted.
Define the polynomial column matrix
\[
 \boxed{\qquad Z_k=\operatorname{diag}(d_h)W_k
             \quad\hbox{in the frame }(1,S',\ldots,S'^{a-v-1}).\qquad}
 \tag{FEX27}
\]
Then $\mathcal C_AK=\psi\operatorname{im}Z_k$. In fact, for a high
coordinate $z$ in FEX26 the equation
$\Xi_{\rm lo}\ell+\Xi_{\rm hi}z=0$ has a solution. Its different
solutions differ by $K\cap L$; FEX24 kills that ambiguity and gives
precisely $\psi Z_k$. Thus this is the actual image, including the
original unit and period dependence in $\Xi$ and the conductor
coefficients. The inverse finite-symbol factor no longer appears in the
columns $Z_k$.

For every $j\ge0$ define the exact transformed relation polynomial
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 R_j^A(S')=\frac{\mathcal C_A(\chi S^j)(S')}{\psi(S')}
 =\frac{v!}{\mu_v}\sum_\nu a_\nu
       \frac{\chi(S'+b_\nu)}{\psi(S')}(S'+b_\nu)^j.
 \quad}\tag{FEX28}
\]
Every displayed quotient is a polynomial. Indeed, if $S'$ is the
$(a',b')$ inner-grid root, then $S'+b_{r_0s_0}$ is the original root
with indices $(a'+r_0,b'+s_0)$. All these indices are between $0$ and $k$.
The degree of $R_j^A$ is $a-v+j$ and its leading coefficient is
$(q+j)_v$; this follows from the first nonzero derivative in FEX17.
It is nonzero, and these distinct degrees prove linear independence of
the relation columns. In particular the high-source terms have not
been replaced by an unjustified continuation of the low-degree symbol.

At endpoint $N$ put $m_N^{\rm pol}=N-v-q'$ and $d_N^{\rm rel}=N+1-q$.
Form the complete polynomial Gram $H_{N,s}^{\psi}$ of
$(1,S',\ldots,S'^{m_N^{\rm pol}})$ in the measure
$|\psi(c'+iy)|^2dm_{0,s}(y)$ at $S'=c'+iy$. Zero-extend $Z_k$ to this
frame and let $R_N^A$ have columns $R_0^A,\ldots,R_{d_N^{\rm rel}-1}^A$.
Define
\[
\begin{split}
 \widehat H_{K,N}^{(s)}={}&Z_k^*H_{N,s}^{\psi}Z_k\\
 &-Z_k^*H_{N,s}^{\psi}R_N^A
    ((R_N^A)^*H_{N,s}^{\psi}R_N^A)^{-1}
                (R_N^A)^*H_{N,s}^{\psi}Z_k,\\
 \widehat F_k^{(s)}={}&
 \sum_{i=0}^3\epsilon_i\log\det\widehat H_{K,N_i}^{(s)},\quad
 (N_0,N_1,N_2,N_3)=(q-1,q,2q-1,2q),\quad
 (\epsilon_0,\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,\epsilon_3)=(1,1,-1,-1).
\end{split}\tag{FEX29}
\]
The empty relation inverse is absent at $N=q-1$. The four relation
ranks are still exactly $0,1,q,q+1$. They have not been truncated to the
smaller kernel dimension. Positivity follows because a nonzero linear
combination of $Z_k$ has degree at most $a-v-1$, whereas every nonzero
combination of the $R_j^A$ has degree at least $a-v$. The complete Gram
is positive in the original positive Gamma density. Minimization over
an increasing relation span proves
\[
 \widehat H_{K,q-1}^{(s)}\succeq\widehat H_{K,q}^{(s)}
 \succeq\cdots,\qquad \widehat F_k^{(s)}\ge0.
 \tag{FEX30}
\]
A change of the fixed basis $W_k$ gives the same four-endpoint value;
its four identical Gram factors cancel with the original signs.

\section{A finite error for the actual compressed determinant}
\label{sec:FEX-error}
Let $K^+=K+L\subset E$. This is only an auxiliary space for an exact
metric calculation, not an enlargement of the observation kernel.
All quotient and restriction metrics below are induced from the same
original $G_N^{(s)}$ and their indicated fixed coefficient frames.
Let $F_{K^+/L}$ and $F_{K^+/K}$ denote their four-endpoint volumes.
The two block Gram factorizations of $K^+$ give
\[
 \boxed{\qquad F_K=F_{K^+/L}+F_L-F_{K^+/K}.\qquad}
 \tag{FEX31}
\]
Before summing there are fixed basis Jacobians; they cancel only after
all four signs. Both factorizations use the actual Schur complements.
The two subquotient dimensions are $\dim L=v$ and
$\dim(K^+/K)=v-t_0$. The existing full AKS covariance inequality passes
by restriction and minimization to every fixed subquotient. Thus, with
$\mathcal L_s=\mathcal L_{s,q}+\mathcal L_{s,q+1}$ from AKS,
\[
 0\le F_L\le v\mathcal L_s,\qquad
 0\le F_{K^+/K}\le(v-t_0)\mathcal L_s.
 \tag{FEX32}
\]
No angle condition between $K$ and $L$ is used.

For a fully explicit existing allowance one may use the AKS Newton
bound in place of a sharper available $\mathcal L_s$. Write
\[
\begin{gathered}
 R=k\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2},\quad
 t_q=\pi/2-1/q,\quad a_q=2\log3/t_q,\quad
 s_q=(a_q^q-1)/(a_q-1),\\
 b_{s,q}=[(9/25)\sin(1/q)]^{-s/2}
          \exp(2R(\log3+t_q/2)),\\
 \mathcal L_{s,j}=\log\left(1+b_{s,q}s_q^2
                  \sum_{d=q}^{q+j-1}\frac{d!}{(s/2)_d}(25/16)^d\right).
\end{gathered}\tag{FEX33}
\]
These are the original complete coefficient bounds with both masses
retained before norm-ratio cancellation. They satisfy
$\mathcal L_s=O_{\delta,\gamma}(q)$ for $s=1,k$ along this family.
Indeed $\log s_q=O(q)$, the last geometric-weighted sum has logarithm
$O(q+\log q)$ because $d!/(s/2)_d\le2\sqrt d$, and
$\log b_{s,q}=O(k\log q+R)=o(q)+O(q)$.

Apply FEX6 to the source $\mathcal P_N/L$ and its conductor image.
The relation subspace is $(\chi\mathcal P_{N-q}+L)/L$. The larger
flag term is generated also by $K$, giving quotient dimension $t$.
By FEX28, its image is the span of $\psi R_N^A$ and $\psi Z_k$.
Multiplication by $\psi$ is an exact isometry from the indicated
weighted coefficient space onto this polynomial image. The source
quotient metric is exactly the metric of $K^+/L$, since successive
minimization first by $\chi\mathcal P_{N-q}$ and then by $L$ is
minimization over their sum. Thus, in the fixed transported frames, put
\[
\begin{gathered}
 e_N=\log\det\widehat H_{K,N}^{(s)}-
                    \log\det H_{K^+/L,N}^{(s)},\qquad n_N=N+1-v,\\
 e^-_{N,s}=\zeta_{N,s}-2(n_N-t)m_N,\quad e^+_{N,s}=2tm_N,
 \quad e^-_{N,s}\le e_N\le e^+_{N,s},\\
 D_s^-=e^-_{q-1,s}+e^-_{q,s}-e^+_{2q-1,s}-e^+_{2q,s},\qquad
 D_s^+=e^+_{q-1,s}+e^+_{q,s}-e^-_{2q-1,s}-e^-_{2q,s}.
\end{gathered}\tag{FEX34}
\]
The signs on $e_{N,s}^{\pm}$ denote new finite scalar bounds; they do not
redefine an original source scalar or covariance. All endpoint quantities are computed from FEX18--20 and the
actual finite ranks in FEX25. Original frame factors have already been
accounted for by transported quotient frames. Combining the four
inequalities and FEX31--32 proves the central finite result:
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \widehat F_k^{(s)}-D_s^+-(v-t_0)\mathcal L_s
 \ \le F_K^{(s)}\le\
 \widehat F_k^{(s)}-D_s^-+v\mathcal L_s.
 \quad}\tag{FEX35}
\]
This is a bound for the actual kernel determinant, not for a different
ambient determinant. Every residual coefficient and relation cross
term remains in FEX29.

For a simpler explicit error let
\[
 J_{\max,s}=\max_{i=0}^3|\zeta_{N_i,s}|,\quad
 m_{\max}=m_{2q},\quad
 \mathcal E_{k,s}=v\mathcal L_s+2J_{\max,s}+2(4q+1)m_{\max}.
 \tag{FEX36}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{|F_K^{(s)}-\widehat F_k^{(s)}|\le\mathcal E_{k,s}
              =O_{\mathsf H,\delta,\gamma}(q\log q)=o(kq).}
 \tag{FEX37}
\]
To check the finite factors, the lower signed bound for $\sum\epsilon_i e_{N_i}$
is at least $-2J_{\max,s}-2(2q+1-2v)m_{\max}$, and the upper bound is at
most $2J_{\max,s}+2(4q+1-2v)m_{\max}$. Enlarge to FEX36 and use
FEX32. Also
\[
 m_{\max}\le
 \log\max\{1,v!A_*^{\rm abs}/|\mu_v|\}
 +8\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2}(H_{2q}+2).
 \tag{FEX38}
\]
Together with FEX20 and FEX33 this proves the order claim. All constants
are fixed at the actual fixed period. Dividing by $kq$ uses
$\log q/k\to0$. A uniform claim over periods approaching a locus where
$\mu_v$ vanishes is not made: the displayed inverse coefficient must
remain in the finite bound. Uniformity holds on a fixed coefficient
stratum with this coefficient ratio bounded and the same $v$.

It follows in particular that $F_K^{(s)}/(kq)$ and
$\widehat F_k^{(s)}/(kq)$ have exactly the same limit points. This does
\emph{not} assert that either sequence has a unique limit. The old
uniform ceiling for $F_K$ remains true, while FEX35--37 constitute a
new, fixed-period transfer at strictly smaller error scale.

\section{The exact closed equilibrium coefficient}
\label{sec:closed-equilibrium-intake}

This section retains the potential, measure, and energy of EIQ1--33:
\begin{equation}\tag{ECL1}
\begin{gathered}
V_{\alpha,\beta}(x)=\beta\sqrt{x}-\alpha\log x,\qquad
\alpha>0,\quad\beta>0,\quad x>0,\\
\mu_{\alpha,\beta}(dx)=\rho_{\alpha,\beta}(x)\,dx,\qquad
F(\alpha,\beta)=
\iint\log|x-y|\,d\mu_{\alpha,\beta}(x)d\mu_{\alpha,\beta}(y)
-\int V_{\alpha,\beta}\,d\mu_{\alpha,\beta},\\
\mathcal L(\alpha,\beta)=\int\log x\,d\mu_{\alpha,\beta}(x).
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
The preceding complete EIQ proof supplies the unique minimizing
probability measure, its positive density and exact support
$[a,b]=[u^2,v^2]$, and its Euler equality. In particular, no assertion
in this section changes the minimization problem or chooses another
measure. The endpoints are exactly
\begin{equation}\tag{ECL2}
uK(k)=\frac{\alpha\pi}{\beta},\qquad
vE(k)=\frac{(\alpha+2)\pi}{\beta},\qquad
k^2=1-\frac{u^2}{v^2},\qquad 0<u<v.
\end{equation}
Here $K$ and $E$ have the modulus convention of EIQ2, not the
elliptic-parameter convention. Define the original endpoint quantities
\begin{equation}\tag{ECL3}
w=\frac{u+v}{2},\qquad z=uv,\qquad
c_{\mathrm{cap}}=\frac{v^2-u^2}{4},\qquad
d\nu(x)=\frac{dx}{\pi\sqrt{(b-x)(x-a)}}\quad(a<x<b).
\end{equation}
The letter $z$ in ECL3 is a positive scalar. A Cauchy-transform variable
below is denoted by $\lambda$. The measure $\nu$ has mass one by
$x=(a+b)/2+(b-a)\cos\theta/2$, $0\leq\theta\leq\pi$.

\subsection{Arcsine identities with their original constants}

Put $m=(a+b)/2$, $d=(b-a)/2$, and $\eta=(v-u)/(v+u)$.
Then $0<\eta<1$ and
\[
x=m+d\cos\theta
 =w^2(1+2\eta\cos\theta+\eta^2),\qquad
z=w^2(1-\eta^2).
\]
The absolutely uniformly convergent series
\[
\begin{split}
\log x&=2\log w+
  2\sum_{n\geq1}\frac{(-1)^{n+1}\eta^n}{n}\cos(n\theta),\\
\frac1x&=\frac1z\left(1+
  2\sum_{n\geq1}(-\eta)^n\cos(n\theta)\right)
\end{split}
\]
follow from the geometric series and the integral of that series.
Termwise integration, and orthogonality of the cosines, prove
\begin{equation}\tag{ECL4}
\begin{split}
\int\log x\,d\nu(x)&=2\log w,\qquad
\int\frac{d\nu(x)}x=\frac1z,\\
\int\frac{\log x}{x}\,d\nu(x)
 &=\frac{2\log w+2\log(1-\eta^2)}z
 =\frac{2\log z-2\log w}z.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
In the product of the two Fourier series, the contribution of degree
$n\geq1$ to the constant coefficient is
$-2\eta^{2n}/(nz)$, giving the displayed logarithm without an omitted
constant.

The logarithmic potential of $\nu$ on its entire support is
\begin{equation}\tag{ECL5}
\int_a^b\log|x-t|\,d\nu(x)=\log c_{\mathrm{cap}},
\qquad a\leq t\leq b.
\end{equation}
Here is a direct proof, including the endpoint values. Write
$t=m+d\cos\phi$ and use
\[
|m+d\cos\theta-t|
=\frac d2
 |e^{i\theta}-e^{i\phi}|\,
 |e^{i\theta}-e^{-i\phi}|.
\]
The integrand depending on $\cos\theta$ has the same mean on
$[0,\pi]$ as on $[0,2\pi]$. For $0<r<1$, the power series of
$\log|1-re^{i\theta}|$ has zero circle mean. This mean tends to
the mean at $r=1$: near its only singular angle,
$|1-re^{i\theta}|^2=(1-r)^2+2r(1-\cos\theta)$,
so for $r\geq1/2$ the absolute value of its negative logarithm
is bounded by $C+|\log|\theta||$, and its positive logarithm
is bounded by $\log2$. These are integrable bounds. A rotation
proves that each of the two circle means above is zero, for
every $\phi$, including $\phi=0,\pi$. Hence their sum is
$\log(d/2)=\log c_{\mathrm{cap}}$, proving ECL5.

All logarithmic double integrals used below are absolutely integrable.
In fact the absolute logarithm for two arcsine variables is bounded by
a constant plus
\[
\left|\log\left|\sin\frac{\theta-\phi}{2}\right|\right|
+\left|\log\left|\sin\frac{\theta+\phi}{2}\right|\right|.
\]
Each term is integrable on $[0,\pi]^2$; near a zero, use
$\sin t\geq 2t/\pi$ for $0\leq t\leq\pi/2$, and integrate
$|\log t|$. Thus the same assertion holds for any two signed
measures whose absolute values are bounded by constant multiples
of $\nu$. The EIQ density also has this domination, because
$\rho(x)/[1/(\pi\sqrt{(b-x)(x-a)})]$ is bounded on $[a,b]$.

Let $\ell$ have the exact EIQ17 convention
\[
V_{\alpha,\beta}(x)
-2\int\log|x-t|\,d\mu_{\alpha,\beta}(t)=\ell
\quad(a\leq x\leq b).
\]
Integrating this equality against $\nu$, using ECL4--5 and
EIQ7, gives
\begin{equation}\tag{ECL6}
\boxed{\displaystyle
\ell=2(\alpha+2)-2\alpha\log w-2\log c_{\mathrm{cap}}.}
\end{equation}
Indeed $\int\sqrt{x}\,d\nu(x)=2vE(k)/\pi$, whose product with
$\beta$ is $2(\alpha+2)$ by ECL2. Fubini is justified by the
absolute integrability just proved and the unit mass of $\mu$.
Smoothness of $\ell$ now follows from the endpoint smoothness in EIQ6.

\subsection{Differentiation with the moving endpoints retained}

All derivatives in this subsection are with respect to $\alpha$ at
fixed $\beta$. Put
\[
p_\alpha(x)=\frac{h_{\alpha,\beta}(x)}{2\pi},\qquad
D(x)=(b-x)(x-a).
\]
In this subsection a dot denotes a parameter derivative, so that
$\dot p(x)$ differentiates the function $p_\alpha(x)$ at fixed $x$.
The function $h_{\alpha,\beta}$ is exactly EIQ10; the subscript on
$p_\alpha$ labels the parameter and does not denote differentiation.
EIQ10 and EIQ29 prove that $p_\alpha$ and its parameter and spatial
derivatives are bounded on a fixed positive compact neighbourhood
of the supports when parameters range in a sufficiently small
compact neighbourhood.

The derivative of the probability measure, interpreted by integration
against every continuously differentiable function on this neighbourhood,
is the finite signed measure
\begin{equation}\tag{ECL7}
\begin{split}
\sigma(dx)&=\left[
\dot p(x)\sqrt{D(x)}
+\frac{p_\alpha(x)}{2\sqrt{D(x)}}
 \{\dot b(x-a)-\dot a(b-x)\}\right]\mathbf1_{(a,b)}(x)\,dx,\\
\frac{\partial}{\partial\alpha}\int f\,d\mu_{\alpha,\beta}
&=\int f\,d\sigma,\qquad \sigma([a,b])=0.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
This identity includes the moving support. To prove it without
postulating endpoint terms, set $\delta=b-a$ and $x=a+\delta y$.
The measure in the fixed variable $y$ is
\[
\delta^2 p_\alpha(a+\delta y)\sqrt{y(1-y)}\,dy.
\]
Its differentiated integral against $f$ is
\[
\int_0^1\sqrt{y(1-y)}
\left[
2\delta\dot\delta\,p_\alpha f
+\delta^2(\dot p+p_\alpha'\dot x)f
+\delta^2p_\alpha f'\dot x
\right]dy,\qquad \dot x=\dot a+\dot\delta y.
\]
Replace $\delta f'$ in the last summand by $d f(x)/dy$ and
integrate by parts. Its boundary term is
$[\delta p_\alpha(x)\dot x\sqrt{y(1-y)}f(x)]_0^1=0$.
The remaining terms combine, on returning to $x$, to
$\dot p\sqrt D+p_\alpha\dot D/(2\sqrt D)$, where
$\dot D=\dot b(x-a)-\dot a(b-x)$, exactly ECL7.
This integration by parts is justified first on
$[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]$ and then by passage to the limit:
the boundary expression tends to zero and the differentiated
square-root factor is bounded by a constant times
$[y(1-y)]^{-1/2}$, an integrable function. The differentiated
fixed-interval integral is valid by the uniform bounds above.
Taking $f=1$ proves the zero total mass in ECL7.
The displayed density also proves $|\sigma|\leq C\nu$.
In particular no endpoint atom has appeared or been discarded.

# Full independent mathematical review of OOQ1–40

Status: **ACCEPTED**, 2026-09-15. Reviewer: /root/conductor_inverse_estimate.

The entire source ORIGINAL_OUTER_QUOTIENT_OPERATOR_CONTROL.tex was read and checked at SHA-256 **6a8510fe1b19a0ae8d45789247ee6c4349d78055098e26670ef80f61bb52f528**, 23549 bytes. This includes all numbered formulas OOQ1–40, every intervening proof, and the final paragraph stating the exact remaining residual comparison. No correction is required.

This review uses the previously fully reviewed CTV1–22, OSP1–35, OFV1–32, EIQ1–33, and QLG1–32 providers. The complete relevant OSP16–29 source-form comparison and OFV1–13 Gamma recurrence/comparison were reread directly for this proof. The companion endpoint-square audit independently checked the finite high-parameter rectangle, mean-value constants, Legendre/translation factors, and low-endpoint extra relation column.

Acceptance concerns the operator theorem for the actual outer quotient and its specified fixed subquotients. It does not identify the original residual graph with the outer ideal, assign a leading value to the separate residual sum, certify a new public edition, or extend any domain.

## 1. Original quotient and source (OOQ1–2)

The parameters remain
\[
k=4l+1,\quad q=(k+1)^2,\quad q'=(k-7)^2,\quad
d=q-q'=16k-48,\quad n=q/2,\quad \vartheta=\pi/2.
\]
The actual root polynomials are
\[
P_k(y)=i^{-q}\chi_k(c+iy),\quad
P_{k-8}(y)=i^{-q'}\chi_{k-8}(c'+iy),\quad
c=k/2,\quad c'=c-4.
\]
CTV's literal central-root inclusion proves \(P_k=P_{k-8}P_{\partial,k}\), with unchanged roots. The outer polynomial is monic of degree \(d\), each root has modulus at most \(R=k\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2}\), and the target is its original increasing-power remainder frame.

The four source degrees are \(L=d-1,d,q+d-1,q+d\). Their full source is
\[
|P_{k-8}(y)|^2dm_s(y),\qquad
dm_s(y)=\frac{(2\pi)^{s/2}2^{s/2}}{4\pi\Gamma(s/2)}
|\Gamma(s/4+iy/2)|^2dy,\quad s=1,k.
\]
The quotient Gram is the minimum over the actual affine remainder fiber at each \(L\), not merely a matrix having the same determinant. All these norms are strictly positive on nonzero polynomials; the remainder map is onto already at \(L=d-1\), so each target Gram is positive definite.

## 2. Compact equilibrium constants (OOQ3–6)

The rectangle is \(\mathcal K=[3/2,5/2]\times[\pi/4,\pi]\), inside the proved positive EIQ parameter quadrant. The exact equilibrium potential satisfies
\[
V(x)-2P(x)=\ell+D(x),\qquad D\ge0,\qquad D|_{[a,b]}=0.
\]
The support endpoints remain in a compact subset of \((0,\infty)\), with a positive minimum gap, and the densities are uniformly bounded. These follow from the explicit EIQ endpoint and density formulas and their proved parameter smoothness. Thus \(a_*>0\), \(B_*<\infty\), \(b_*>0\), \(M_*<\infty\), and the specified bound \(L_*\) for \(V'\) is finite.

For \(x>0\), the positive logarithmic part gives
\[
P(x)\le\log(1+x)+\log(1+B_*).
\]
The negative part has integral at most
\[
M_*\int_{-1}^1-\log|u|\,du=2M_*,
\]
so \(P(x)\ge-2M_*\). Evaluating the Euler equality on the compact support bounds \(\ell\). For \(x\ge1\) this proves the stated uniform lower estimate
\[
D(x)\ge(\pi/4)\sqrt x-(5/2)\log x-2\log(1+x)-C.
\]
Near zero the compact support is bounded away from zero, so \(P\) is uniformly bounded and \(-\alpha\log x\to+\infty\) uniformly. The tail therefore proves both finiteness of \(C_{\rm tail}\) and integrability defining \(T_*\); on the compact remaining interval \(D\ge0\) suffices. A constant multiple of \((1+x)^2(1+x^{5/2})e^{-\pi\sqrt x/4}\) is an integrable majorant. These constants do not conceal an assumed tail theorem.

The relation defining \(W\) has the correct sign. Integrating the Euler equality gives \(\ell=\int V-2I\), where \(I=\iint\log|x-y|\,d\mu d\mu\), while \(F=I-\int V\). Thus
\[
\ell/2=-F-\tfrac12\int V.
\]
EIQ proves \(P_0=F_\alpha\) and \(\beta\int\sqrt x\,d\mu=2(\alpha+1)\), whence
\[
\int V=2(\alpha+1)-\alpha F_\alpha,\qquad
W=P_0+\ell/2=-F-(\alpha+1)+(1+\alpha/2)F_\alpha.
\]
EIQ parameter smoothness gives bounded first derivatives of \(W\) on \(\mathcal K\), so the explicit \(C_W\) is finite.

## 3. Polynomial evaluation in every direction (OOQ7–8)

Let \(m\ge\max\{1,2/b_*\}\), \(\deg p\le m\), and
\[
M=\max_{[a,b]}|p(x)|e^{-mV(x)/2}.
\]
For nonzero \(p\), choose a maximizing \(x_0\). One of the two sides inside \([a,b]\) has length at least \(1/m\). On that interval \(J\),
\[
|p(x)|\le e^{L_*/2}|p(x_0)|.
\]
The complex-coefficient Chebyshev expansion on the affine copy of \([-1,1]\) has coefficients of modulus at most \(2\|p\|_{\infty,J}\), while \(|T_j'|\le j^2\). Since \(\sum_{j=1}^m j^2\le m^3\), including \(m=1\), the affine derivative factor gives
\[
\|p'\|_{\infty,J}\le4m^3|J|^{-1}\|p\|_{\infty,J}.
\]
Here \(|J|=1/m\). On a one-sided segment of length \([8e^{L_*/2}m^4]^{-1}\), the polynomial consequently differs from \(p(x_0)\) by at most half its modulus. The weight there is at least \(e^{-L_*}e^{-mV(x_0)}\). Integrating proves
\[
\|p\|_{m,V}^2\ge\frac{M^2}{32e^{3L_*/2}m^4},
\quad
M\le C_{\rm BM}m^2\|p\|_{m,V}.
\]

Off the interval, \(\log|p(z)|-mP(z)\) is subharmonic. On its boundary the Euler equality bounds it above by \(\log M+m\ell/2\). In the coordinate \(w=1/z\), its possible singularity at infinity is \((m-\deg p)\log|w|\) plus a harmonic function, hence it extends subharmonically. The maximum principle on the interval complement in the sphere gives the same upper bound everywhere off the interval. Bounded density makes \(P\) continuous at the boundary. The zero polynomial satisfies the resulting inequality directly. Thus
\[
|p(z)|\le C_{\rm BM}m^2e^{m(P(z)+\ell/2)}\|p\|_{m,V}.
\]
For \(|z|\le a_*/2\), each support point obeys
\[
|\log|1-z/t||\le2|z|/a_*,
\]
so \(|P(z)-P_0|\le2|z|/a_*\). This proves OOQ8 with its exact exponent. This lower-lift norm estimate applies to every polynomial, not just a chosen orthogonal direction.

## 4. Quantile polynomial lift (OOQ9–11)

The actual equilibrium's \(n\) consecutive mass-\(1/n\) intervals have total length at most \(B_*\). Their midpoints \(\xi_i\) define
\[
r_n(x)=\prod_{i=1}^n(1-x/\xi_i),\qquad r_n(0)=1.
\]
For \(f_\eta(t)=\log\max\{|x-t|,\eta\}\), the Lipschitz constant is \(1/\eta\). Comparing each midpoint with \(n\) times the integral over its mass interval gives total absolute error at most \(B_*/\eta\). The truncated logarithmic singularity contributes at most \(2nM_*\eta\). With \(\eta=n^{-1/2}\), the sum is \((B_*+2M_*)\sqrt n\). Finally \(\log t\) has Lipschitz constant \(1/a_*\) on the support, giving
\[
\left|\sum_i\log\xi_i-nP_0\right|\le B_*/a_*.
\]
These estimates prove
\[
\log|r_n(x)|\le n(P(x)-P_0)+C_{\rm quant}\sqrt n+C_0.
\]
At a root the left side is minus infinity, so the same inequality holds.

For complex \(|z|\le a_*/2\), the individual inequality
\[
|1-z/\xi_i|\ge1-|z|/a_*\ge e^{-2|z|/a_*}
\]
gives \(|r_n(z)|^{-1}\le e^{2n|z|/a_*}\). This is the needed analytic inverse bound on the complete disk; no zero is moved or ignored.

## 5. Exact remainder and all its coefficient factors (OOQ12–15)

With \(\rho=n^{-1/8}\), \(\widehat P(z)=n^{-d}P_{\partial,k}(nz)\), and \(r_*=R/n\), OOQ13 imposes
\[
n\ge2d+1,\quad n\ge2/b_*,\quad r_*\le\rho/2,\quad
\rho\le\min\{1/2,\sqrt{a_*/2}\},
\]
together with OSP23 and \(k\ge257\). All are eventual for the fixed original quartet, since \(n\asymp k^2\), \(d=O(k)\), and \(r_*=O(k^{-1})\).

For a function holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed disk, the displayed contour formula is a polynomial of degree at most \(d-1\). At any original root of \(\widehat P\), Cauchy's formula returns the function value. The original simple-quartet roots are distinct, so these \(d\) values uniquely determine the remainder; the formula agrees with ordinary division on polynomials.

On the contour, \(|\widehat P(\zeta)|\ge(\rho-r_*)^d\ge(\rho/2)^d\). Expanding the divided difference gives the exact coefficient polynomial
\[
\sum_{a=1}^dp_a\sum_{h=0}^{a-1}\zeta^{a-1-h}z^h.
\]
Because \(\rho\le1\), its coefficient norm is at most \(d\sum_a|p_a|\), and the entire monic product has coefficient sum at most \((1+r_*)^d\). The contour length divided by \(2\pi\) contributes \(\rho\), proving
\[
\|\operatorname{rem}_{\widehat P}f\|_1
\le C_{\rm rem}\max_{|\zeta|=\rho}|f(\zeta)|,\quad
C_{\rm rem}=\rho d(1+r_*)^d(2/\rho)^d.
\]
Its logarithm is \(O(d\log n+\log d)\). Every coefficient of the actual outer root polynomial remains in the map.

## 6. High-degree lower bound (OOQ16–20)

The comparison source is \(|y|^{2Q}e^{-\beta|y|}dy\), with \(Q=q'+\ell_s\), \(\ell_s=(s-1)/4\), and \(\beta=\vartheta\pm1/q\). Let
\[
\alpha_0=(Q-\tfrac12)/n,\qquad
c_{\rm high}=(2Q+1)\log n-2nW(\alpha_0,\beta).
\]
At \(L=q+d-1\), the two parity degrees are both \(n+d/2-1\). At \(L=q+d\), they are \(n+d/2\) and \(n+d/2-1\). In particular \(n\le m_e,m_o\le n+d\).

The exact parity parameters are
\[
(\alpha_e,\beta_e)=((Q-\tfrac12)/m_e,n\beta/m_e),\quad
(\alpha_o,\beta_o)=((Q+\tfrac12)/m_o,n\beta/m_o).
\]
The inequalities \(d/q<1/16\), \(\ell_s/q<1/64\), and the actual rounding prove that these and \((\alpha_0,\beta)\) lie in \(\mathcal K\). For example the alpha parameters lie above \(5/3-8/(9q)>3/2\) and below \(2+1/32+1/q<5/2\); using \(1/q<\pi/8\) gives rates between \(\pi/3\) and \(5\pi/8\), inside the retained rectangle.

Writing \(p(nz)=p_e(z^2)+zp_o(z^2)\), cancellation of the odd cross terms between \(z=\sqrt x\) and \(z=-\sqrt x\) gives exactly
\[
n^{-(2Q+1)}\|p\|_{\exp}^2
=\int|p_e(x)|^2x^{Q-1/2}e^{-n\beta\sqrt x}dx
+\int|p_o(x)|^2x^{Q+1/2}e^{-n\beta\sqrt x}dx.
\]
Each half-axis contributes \(1/(2\sqrt x)\), so no factor two is absent.

For either parity, \(|m-n|\le d+1\),
\[
m|\alpha-\alpha_0|\le1+(5/2)|m-n|,\qquad
m|\beta_m-\beta|\le\pi|m-n|.
\]
The mean-value formula on the rectangle, together with the specified \(C_W\), proves
\[
|mW(\alpha,\beta_m)-nW(\alpha_0,\beta)|\le C_W(d+2).
\]
Applying OOQ8 at \(x=\zeta^2\), then \(|\zeta|=\rho\le1\), Cauchy–Schwarz in the two parity norms, and the remainder bound yields
\[
\|v\|_2\le C_{\rm rem}\sqrt2C_{\rm BM}(n+d)^2
e^{nW+C_W(d+2)+2(n+d)\rho^2/a_*}
n^{-(2Q+1)/2}\|p\|_{\exp}.
\]
This holds for every lift with remainder \(v\). Squaring and rearranging gives the lower target-form bound with exactly \(E_{\rm high}^-\) in OOQ24.

## 7. High-degree upper bound and coordinate transport (OOQ21–25)

For a prescribed degree-less-than-\(d\) remainder \(v(z)\), form the actual analytic remainder
\[
a_v=\operatorname{rem}_{\widehat P}\bigl(v/r_n(z^2)\bigr),\qquad
p_v(nz)=r_n(z^2)a_v(z).
\]
The denominator has no zero in the disk because its squared-coordinate roots are at least \(a_*>\rho^2\). This polynomial has degree at most \(2n+d-1=q+d-1\), admitted at both high endpoints. Its values at all actual outer roots equal \(v\), so it is an actual lift.

On the contour, \(|v(\zeta)|\le\sqrt d\|v\|_2\), and OOQ11 gives
\[
\|a_v\|_1\le C_{\rm rem}\sqrt d\,e^{2n\rho^2/a_*}\|v\|_2.
\]
On either real half-axis,
\[
|a_v(\pm\sqrt x)|\le\|a_v\|_1(1+\sqrt x)^{d-1}.
\]
The definition of \(C_{\rm tail}\) implies
\[
(1+\sqrt x)^{2(d-1)}
\le e^{2C_{\rm tail}(d-1)}e^{2(d-1)D(x)}.
\]
The quantile bound and \(2P-V=-\ell-D\) then leave
\[
e^{-2nP_0-n\ell}\,e^{-[n-2(d-1)]D(x)}
=e^{-2nW}\,e^{-[n-2(d-1)]D(x)}.
\]
Since \(n-2(d-1)\ge1\), integration is bounded by \(T_*\). The exact \(y=nz\) Jacobian/power factor is \(n^{2Q+1}\), giving OOQ23 and precisely \(E_{\rm high}^+\).

If \(w\) is the original \(y\)-remainder coefficient vector, its scaled vector is
\[
v=D_nw,\qquad D_n=\operatorname{diag}(1,n,\ldots,n^{d-1}).
\]
Indeed division after the literal substitution has remainder \(v(z)=\sum w_jn^jz^j\). Therefore
\[
Q_{\rm original}=D_n^*Q_{\rm scaled}D_n,\qquad
I\preceq D_n^*D_n\preceq n^{2(d-1)}I.
\]
Adding \(2(d-1)\log n\) to the maximum of the two scalar errors proves OOQ25 in the original frame. Since \(n\rho^2=n^{3/4}\), \(\sqrt n\le n^{3/4}\), and \(\log C_{\rm rem}=O(d\log n)\), the high error is \(O(n^{3/4}+d\log n)\).

## 8. Low degrees and the complete additional ideal column (OOQ26–29)

Let \(y_0=2Q/\beta\) and \(g(Q,\beta)=2Q\log(2Q/\beta)-2Q\). On \([y_0,y_0+1]\), the weight is at least \(e^{g(Q,\beta)-\beta}\).

On \([0,1]\), the orthonormal shifted Legendre polynomial of degree \(j\) has coefficient sum at most \(\sqrt{2j+1}\,8^j\): Rodrigues' coefficients are \((-1)^{j-r}\binom jr\binom{j+r}r\), whose absolute sum is at most \(2^j4^j\). The Euclidean operator norm of their complete coefficient matrix is therefore at most
\[
\sqrt{(d+1)(2d+1)}\,8^d.
\]
The translation of coefficient vectors by \(-y_0\) has norm at most \(\sqrt{d+1}(1+y_0)^d\). Multiplying these two bounds, and then squaring, proves the lower Gram denominator
\[
(d+1)^2(2d+1)64^d(1+y_0)^{2d}
\]
in OOQ26. It is a form bound on every coefficient vector.

The upper form bound is the trace, exactly
\[
\sum_{j=0}^d2(2Q+2j)!/\beta^{2Q+2j+1}.
\]
At \(L=d-1\) the remainder map is the identity. At \(L=d\) it is exactly \([I_d,-p_{\rm low}]\), with every lower coefficient of \(P_{\partial,k}\). Its norm squared is \(1+\|p_{\rm low}\|_2^2\), bounded by \((d+1)(1+R)^{2d}\). For any lift \(w\) of \(v\), \(\|w\|_2\ge\|v\|_2/\|[I,-p_{\rm low}]\|_2\). Thus the extra factor contributes precisely one further \(\log(d+1)\) and \(2d\log(1+R)\) to the lower-error exponent, as in OOQ28. The canonical lift \((v,0)\) proves the upper quotient bound.

The integral estimates
\[
m\log m-m+1\le\log(m!)\le m\log m-m+1+\log m
\]
show that each trace summand's logarithm exceeds \(g(Q,\beta)\) by at most \(O(d\log(Q+d)+\log(Q+d))\). Summing adds only \(\log(d+1)\). The lower displayed error has that same order, because \(Q\asymp q\), \(d=O(k)\), \(R=O_{\delta,\gamma}(k)\), and the rates remain in a fixed positive interval. This proves both OOQ29 and \(E_{\rm low}=O_{\delta,\gamma}(d\log q)\).

## 9. Complete original source transport and finite error (OOQ30–35)

OSP20–26 is a full polynomial-form comparison between the actual \(P_{k-8}\) multiplier and \(y^{q'}\), preserving the original source order and every root coefficient. Its error is \(\mathcal E_k\). OFV5–7 is the literal recurrence
\[
dm_s=\beta_s\prod_{a=0}^{\ell_s-1}(y^2+t_a^2)d\sigma,\quad
t_a=2a+\tfrac12,\quad
\beta_s=(2\pi)^{s/2}/(\sqrt2\,\Gamma(s/2)),
\]
and the full-form comparison to the \(y^{2\ell_s}\) multiplier has lower ratio one and upper ratio \(e^{r_{\ell_s}}\). The proof includes the inner interval and every multiplier factor. For \(s=1\), \(\beta_1=1\), \(\ell_1=0\), and \(r_0=0\).

The pointwise one-factor Gamma inequalities are
\[
L_he^{-(\vartheta+h)|y|}\le d\sigma/dy

## 1. The original roots, source and full-window rank

Fix the actual simple-quartet and five-orbit data of ROQ, with
\(k=4l+1\ge9\), \(q=(k+1)^2\), \(q'=(k-7)^2\),
\(\Delta=q-q'=16k-48\), \(j=8k-32>0\), and the actual
source order \(s=1\) or \(s=k\).
RWC1 uses exactly ROQ10's original columns
\[
 u_n=\bigl(p_n(\omega_{ab})/\sqrt{h_n}\bigr)_{ab},\qquad
 h_n=(2\pi)^{s/2}n!(s/2)_n,
 \quad \omega_{ab}=(2b-k)\gamma-i(2a-k)\delta .
\]
Both the ordered primary coordinates and the original Gamma
mass remain in these entries. No monic-in-\(S\) column has
been substituted for this original real-coordinate polynomial.

Since \(\delta,\gamma>0\), equality of two roots forces equality
of their real indices and their imaginary indices. They are
distinct. The first \(q\) monic polynomials have an upper
triangular monomial coefficient matrix with nonzero diagonal,
so their evaluation matrix is an invertible Vandermonde times
an invertible triangular matrix and the nonzero norm factors.
Thus \(R_N=\sum_{n=0}^Nu_nu_n^*>0\) for \(N\ge q-1\).

Because \(k\) is odd, the root at \((k-a,b)\) is the complex
conjugate of the root at \((a,b)\), and no \(a=k/2\) occurs.
Pairing exactly these roots gives
\[
 P_k(y)=
 \prod_{a=0}^{(k-1)/2}\prod_{b=0}^k
 \left((y-(2b-k)\gamma)^2+(k-2a)^2\delta^2\right)>0
 \quad(y\in\mathbb R).
\]
The number of paired factors is \(q/2\), each is monic of
degree two, and every original root occurs exactly once.
This verifies the full constant and degree in RWC2.

For any \(N\ge q-1\), suppose
\(U_N^+c=0\), where \(U_N^+=[u_{N+1},\ldots,u_{N+q}]\).
The polynomial
\[
 f(y)=\sum_{a=1}^q c_a p_{N+a}(y)/\sqrt{h_{N+a}}
\]
vanishes at all roots of \(P_k\). Since those roots are distinct,
ordinary polynomial division gives \(f=P_kr\) with \(\deg r\le N\).
Each polynomial in the sum is orthogonal, for the original
positive Gamma measure, to every degree-at-most-\(N\) polynomial.
Therefore
\[
 0=\int f(y)\overline{r(y)}\,dm_s(y)
   =\int P_k(y)|r(y)|^2\,dm_s(y).
\]
The integrals exist by the original polynomial moments. If
\(r\ne0\), its zeros on the real line form a finite set, while
\(P_k\) and the density are strictly positive. The last integral
would be strictly positive. Hence \(r=0\), then \(f=0\).
Distinct monic degrees force every coefficient \(c_a=0\).
Thus \(U_N^+\) is an invertible \(q\times q\) matrix at every
asserted cutoff. This proves RWC3 on the original columns.

## 2. Exact conditioned projection and simultaneous update

ROQ4–7 provides the actual \(C:\mathbb C^q\to\mathbb C^{q'}\)
and \(D:\mathbb C^q\to\mathbb C^j\), with \(C\) onto and
\(D|_{\ker C}\) onto. These are precisely the conductor and
certificate rows used in RWC. Put \(A=CRC^*>0\).
The matrix
\[
 \Pi=I_q-RC^*A^{-1}C
\]
satisfies \(C\Pi=0\), fixes every vector in \(\ker C\), and
kills \(RC^*\mathbb C^{q'}\). If \(\Pi x=0\), then
\(x=RC^*A^{-1}Cx\), proving that its kernel is exactly this
last space. Hence it is the specified projection onto
\(\ker C\). Its metric identity is
\(\Pi^*R^{-1}=R^{-1}\Pi=R^{-1}-C^*A^{-1}C\).
This supplies its exact relationship to the original minimum
metric; no Euclidean orthogonal projection was inserted.

ROQ16 gives \(W=R-RC^*A^{-1}CR\) and
\(\Omega=DWD^*>0\), with the exact quotient metric
\(Q_\Xi=\Omega^{-1}\). In particular the same residual
quotient and its complete denominator are retained.

The dimensions of the new matrices are
\[
 U_N^+:q\times q,\quad X=CU_N^+:q'\times q,\quad
 B=I_q+X^*A^{-1}X:q\times q,\quad
 Z=D\Pi U_N^+:j\times q,\quad V=ZB^{-1}Z^*:j\times j.
\]
The identity matrix makes \(B>0\). Invertibility of \(U_N^+\)
implies \(\operatorname{im}(\Pi U_N^+)=\ker C\), and the
actual surjection \(D|_{\ker C}\) therefore gives
\(\operatorname{rank}Z=j\). Since \(Z^*\) is injective,
\(y^*Vy=(Z^*y)^*B^{-1}(Z^*y)>0\) for \(y\ne0\).
This proves RWC4–5 without a generic-rank premise.

For the full matrix calculation write \(U=U_N^+\) and
\(T=RC^*A^{-1}X\). Multiplication, using
\((A+XX^*)A^{-1}X=XB\), proves
\[
 (A+XX^*)^{-1}
   =A^{-1}-A^{-1}XB^{-1}X^*A^{-1}.
\]
The complete new covariance product subtracted in \(W_{N+q}\) is
\[
 RC^*A^{-1}CR+TU^*+UT^*+U(B-I_q)U^*
 -[T+U(B-I_q)]B^{-1}[T+U(B-I_q)]^*.
\]
Set \(E=U-T=\Pi U\). The bracket is \(UB-E\), whose product
with \(B^{-1}\) and its adjoint equals
\(UBU^*-UE^*-EU^*+EB^{-1}E^*\).
Subtracting the entire displayed covariance product from
\(R+UU^*\) and then subtracting \(W_N\) cancels the other
terms exactly, leaving \(EB^{-1}E^*\).
Thus
\[
 W_{N+q}-W_N=(\Pi U)B^{-1}(\Pi U)^*,\qquad
 \Omega_{N+q}=\Omega_N+ZB^{-1}Z^*.
\]
Inverting the latter matrix gives RWC6's original
\(Q_{\Xi,N+q}\). All off-diagonal entries of the full
\(q\times q\) denominator \(B\) are present.

## 3. Every exterior coefficient and both finite bounds

The exact map
\[
 Y_N=\Omega_N^{-1/2}Z_NB_N^{-1/2}:\mathbb C^q\to\mathbb C^j
\]
has rank \(j\) in the indicated standard Hermitian spaces.
Its complete Gram is
\[
 T_N=Y_NY_N^*=\Omega_N^{-1/2}V_N\Omega_N^{-1/2}>0.
\]
Consequently \(t_N=\operatorname{Tr}T_N>0\) and
\(c_N=\det T_N=\det V_N/\det\Omega_N>0\), proving RWC7.
The covariance update is the congruence
\(\Omega_{N+q}=\Omega_N^{1/2}(I_j+T_N)\Omega_N^{1/2}\).
Taking determinants therefore gives
\[
 L_N=\log\det(I_j+T_N)
    =\sum_{a=1}^j\log(1+\lambda_a)>0,
\]
where \(\lambda_a>0\) are the actual eigenvalues.

For \(0\le d\le j\), the exact exterior map is
\(\bigwedge^dY_N:\bigwedge^d\mathbb C^q\to
\bigwedge^d\mathbb C^j\). In orthonormal wedge bases,
its singular values squared are the products
\(\prod_{a\in I}\lambda_a\), one for each \(d\)-subset of
the \(j\) nonzero singular directions. Its other singular
directions contribute zero. Thus
\[
 \|\bigwedge^dY_N\|_{\rm HS}^2
   =\sum_{|I|=d}\prod_{a\in I}\lambda_a=e_d(T_N).
\]
Equivalently these are exactly the sums of squared moduli of
all \(d\times d\) minors, including every row and column
selection. The case \(d=0\) is the identity between
one-dimensional exterior-zero spaces and has squared norm one.
The case \(d=j\) is \(c_N\). Expansion of the product
\(\prod_a(1+\lambda_a)\) now proves every RWC8 coefficient.

Keeping only degrees zero and one gives
\(\det(I+T_N)\ge1+t_N\). For \(1\le d\le j\), the product
of all \(\binom jd\) positive \(d\)-fold eigenvalue products
is \(c_N^{\binom{j-1}{d-1}}\). Arithmetic–geometric mean
therefore gives
\[
 e_d(T_N)\ge\binom jd c_N^{d/j}.
\]
For \(d=0\) both sides equal one. Summing these inequalities
gives \(\det(I+T_N)\ge(1+c_N^{1/j})^j\).
Finally the second derivative of \(\log(1+x)\) is
\(-1/(1+x)^2<0\), so its concavity gives
\(\sum_a\log(1+\lambda_a)\le j\log(1+t_N/j)\).
This proves exactly the maximum of the two lower bounds
and the upper bound in RWC9. Each positive partial sum of
the exact exterior coefficients supplies the stated further
lower bound.

## 4. Original endpoints, signs and finite-domain correction

Since \(Q_{\Xi,N}=\Omega_N^{-1}\), the original signed
four-endpoint return is
\[
 \begin{split}
 \Phi_{k,s}
 &=\log\det Q_{\Xi,q-1}+\log\det Q_{\Xi,q}
   -\log\det Q_{\Xi,2q-1}-\log\det Q_{\Xi,2q}\\
 &=L_{q-1}+L_q>0.
 \end{split}
\]
The two windows are exactly \(q-1\to2q-1\) and
\(q\to2q\), both of length \(q\). Their positive bounds
give RWC11's \(\ell_{k,s}\le\Phi_{k,s}\le u_{k,s}\).
ROQ21 supplies the simultaneous interval
\[
 \lambda_s\le\Phi_{k,s}\le
 j(\mathcal L_{s,q}+\mathcal L_{s,q+1})-\lambda_s .
\]
Intersecting the actual intervals proves the stated
\(\Phi^-=\max(\ell,\lambda_s)\) and
\(\Phi^+=\min(u,j(\mathcal L_{s,q}+\mathcal L_{s,q+1})-\lambda_s)\).
Their order is guaranteed by containment of the actual \(\Phi\).

The seven-moment identity is specifically PMR3:
\[
 F_K^{(s)}=\mathcal F_{0,k}^{(s)}-\Phi_{k,s}
                         +\mathfrak e^0_{k,s}.
\]
Its proved finite domain is
\[
 k\ge29,\qquad
 k\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2}\le2^{-33}(k+1)^2,
\]
with the original sequence \(k=4l+1\). Its two finite errors
are exactly
\[
 e_{k,s}^{0,-}=e_{k,s}^-+c_k^\circ,\quad
 e_{k,s}^{0,+}=e_{k,s}^++c_k^\circ,\quad
 -e_{k,s}^{0,-}\le\mathfrak e^0_{k,s}\le e_{k,s}^{0,+}.
\]
Here \(c_k^\circ=4(q+\Delta+1)\mathcal E_k\) is PMR2's
complete same-source root-to-moment allowance. It is added
to each of the unequal OAR2 endpoints; they are not made
equal by this addition.

Substitution of the upper residual bound and the lower error
bound gives
\(\mathcal F_0-e^{0,-}-\Phi^+\le F_K\).
Substitution of the lower residual bound and upper error
bound gives
\(F_K\le\mathcal F_0+e^{0,+}-\Phi^-\).
These are precisely RWC12. Outside the displayed PMR range,
OAR3 gives the same valid operation using
\(\mathcal F_\partial\) and \(e^\pm\), on OAR's original
domain. The final author repair now states this explicitly.
The full-window results RWC1–11 do not require the PMR
threshold and keep their original \(k\ge9\) domain.

For the signed arithmetic return retain OVR's original
AMT period domain \(|u|\ge R_*\) as well. OAR11/PMR7 gives
the exact identity
\[
 \Psi_k=F_K^{(k)}+\mathcal H_k+\delta_k^\sigma
 =\mathcal F_{0,k}^{(k)}-\Phi_{k,k}
   +\mathcal H_k+\delta_k^\sigma+\mathfrak e^0_{k,k}.
\]
Adding these same unchanged scalars to both sides of RWC12
at source order \(k\) proves RWC13. In particular the lower
side subtracts \(e^{0,-}\) and \(\Phi^+\), while the upper
side adds \(e^{0,+}\) and subtracts \(\Phi^-\). The two
Gamma source orders, every arithmetic correction and all
four endpoint orientations are retained.

## 5. The strict improvement over the original first increment

For each individual cutoff \(a\), ROQ18 gives
\(\Omega_{a+1}-\Omega_a=z_az_a^*/a_a\), with \(a_a>0\).
Adding the actual \(q\) steps and comparing with RWC6 yields
\[
 V_{q-1}=\sum_{a=q-1}^{2q-2}z_az_a^*/a_a .
\]
Taking the trace after the original congruence with

\[
 t_{q-1}=\sum_{a=q-1}^{2q-2}
   z_a^*\Omega_{q-1}^{-1}z_a/a_a\ge\eta_{q-1}.
\]
Every term is nonnegative; only the first term is identified
with \(\eta_{q-1}\). The later terms retain their individual
conditioned columns and the fixed base covariance in this

least \(\log(1+\eta_{q-1})=\lambda_s\). The second-window
lower bound is strictly positive because \(V_q>0\).
Their sum proves \(\ell_{k,s}>\lambda_s\).

This independently derived comparison was sent to the author
and is now proved in full as RWC14. Consequently the original
recorded maximum \(\Phi^-=\max(\ell,\lambda_s)\) equals
\(\ell\), with a strict finite improvement of that earlier
first-increment endpoint. It assigns no leading rate to
\(\Phi_{k,s}/(kq)\); the matrices in every formula remain

The final RWC proof reconstructs the reported full-window

"""Exact outward certificate; Python integers only, no floating-point input.

Every interval endpoint is an integer divided by SCALE. All divisions round
outward. Explicit analytic tails enclose the infinite defining series.
Run normally and with -O; correctness checks deliberately do not use assert.
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import hashlib
import json

SCALE = 10 ** 70
ELLIPTIC_TERMS = 3200
ARCTAN_TERMS = 128
LOG_TERMS = 256


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise ArithmeticError(message)


def ceil_div(n, d):
    require(d != 0, "zero denominator")
    if d < 0:
        n, d = -n, -d
    return -((-n) // d)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class I:
    lo: int
    hi: int

    def __post_init__(self):
        require(self.lo <= self.hi, "reversed interval")

    @staticmethod
    def rational(n, d=1):
        require(d != 0, "zero rational denominator")
        if d < 0:
            n, d = -n, -d
        return I(n * SCALE // d, ceil_div(n * SCALE, d))

    @staticmethod
    def decimal(s):
        sign = -1 if s.startswith('-') else 1
        s = s.lstrip('+-')
        whole, dot, frac = s.partition('.')
        return I.rational(sign * int(whole + frac), 10 ** len(frac))

    def __add__(self, other):
        other = to_i(other)
        return I(self.lo + other.lo, self.hi + other.hi)

    __radd__ = __add__

    def __neg__(self):
        return I(-self.hi, -self.lo)

    def __sub__(self, other):
        return self + (-to_i(other))

    def __rsub__(self, other):
        return to_i(other) - self

    def __mul__(self, other):
        other = to_i(other)
        values = [a * b for a in (self.lo, self.hi)
                  for b in (other.lo, other.hi)]
        return I(min(values) // SCALE, ceil_div(max(values), SCALE))

    __rmul__ = __mul__

    def __truediv__(self, other):
        other = to_i(other)
        require(other.lo > 0 or other.hi < 0,
                "division interval contains zero")
        pairs = [(a * SCALE, b) for a in (self.lo, self.hi)
                 for b in (other.lo, other.hi)]
        lows = [n // d for n, d in pairs]
        highs = [ceil_div(n, d) for n, d in pairs]
        return I(min(lows), max(highs))

    def __rtruediv__(self, other):
        return to_i(other) / self

    def power(self, n):
        require(isinstance(n, int) and n >= 0, "nonnegative integer power")
        answer, base = I.rational(1), self
        while n:
            if n & 1:
                answer = answer * base
            base = base * base
            n //= 2
        return answer

    def outward_decimal(self, digits=36):
        factor = 10 ** digits
        left = self.lo * factor // SCALE
        right = ceil_div(self.hi * factor, SCALE)

        def display(value):
            sign = '-' if value < 0 else ''
            value = abs(value)
            return sign + str(value // factor) + '.' + str(value % factor).zfill(digits)

        return [display(left), display(right)]

    def record(self):
        return {"scaled_lower": str(self.lo), "scaled_upper": str(self.hi),
                "outward_decimal_36": self.outward_decimal()}


def to_i(value):
    if isinstance(value, I):
        return value
    require(isinstance(value, int), "noninteger scalar")
    return I.rational(value)


def elliptic_bar(m):
    """Enclose 2K(sqrt(m))/pi and 2E(sqrt(m))/pi, retaining m."""
    require(0 < m.lo and m.hi < SCALE, "elliptic parameter outside (0,1)")
    term = I.rational(1)
    ks = I.rational(1)
    es = I.rational(1)
    for n in range(1, ELLIPTIC_TERMS):
        term = term * m * I.rational((2*n-1)**2, 4*n*n)
        ks = ks + term
        es = es - term / (2*n-1)
    n = ELLIPTIC_TERMS
    next_term = term * m * I.rational((2*n-1)**2, 4*n*n)
    ktail = next_term / (1-m)
    etail = ktail / (2*n-1)
    require(0 <= ktail.lo and 0 <= etail.lo, "negative elliptic tail")
    return (ks + I(0, ktail.hi), es - I(0, etail.hi),
            {"K_bar_tail_upper_scaled": str(ktail.hi),
             "E_bar_tail_upper_scaled": str(etail.hi)})


def atan_reciprocal(q):
    x = I.rational(1, q)
    xx = x*x
    term = x
    total = I.rational(0)
    for n in range(ARCTAN_TERMS):
        contribution = term / (2*n+1)
        total = total + contribution if n % 2 == 0 else total - contribution
        term = term * xx
    bound = term / (2*ARCTAN_TERMS+1)
    # The first omitted alternating term has positive sign for the even N.
    return total + I(0, bound.hi)


def log_interval(x):
    require(x.lo > 0, "nonpositive logarithm argument")
    t = (x-1)/(x+1)
    require(-SCALE < t.lo and t.hi < SCALE, "atanh outside unit interval")
    tt = t*t
    term = t
    total = I.rational(0)
    for n in range(LOG_TERMS):
        total = total + 2*term/(2*n+1)
        term = term*tt
    rvalue = max(abs(t.lo), abs(t.hi))
    r = I(rvalue, rvalue)
    bound = 2*r.power(2*LOG_TERMS+1)/((2*LOG_TERMS+1)*(1-r*r))
    return total + I(-bound.hi, bound.hi)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path,
                        default=Path(__file__).with_name('CERTIFICATE_RECEIPT.json'))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    h_left = I.decimal('0.160101670957718355884567453115')
    h_right = I.decimal('0.160101670957718355884567453116')
    require(h_left.lo == h_left.hi and h_right.lo == h_right.hi,
            "endpoint rationals must be exactly represented")
    signs = {}
    for label, endpoint in [('left', h_left), ('right', h_right)]:
        kb, eb, tail = elliptic_bar(1-endpoint*endpoint)
        residual = 2*endpoint*kb-eb
        signs[label] = {"h": endpoint.record(), "residual": residual.record(),
                        "tails": tail}
        if label == 'left':
            require(residual.hi < 0, "left endpoint sign not certified")
        else:
            require(residual.lo > 0, "right endpoint sign not certified")
    h = I(h_left.lo, h_right.hi)
    m = 1-h*h
    kb, eb, tails = elliptic_bar(m)
    pi = 16*atan_reciprocal(5)-4*atan_reciprocal(239)
    require(pi.lo > 3*SCALE and pi.hi < 4*SCALE, "Machin pi enclosure")
    K = pi*kb/2
    E = pi*eb/2
    v = 4/E
    u = h*v
    w = (u+v)/2
    z = u*v
    cap = (v*v-u*u)/4
    require(u.lo > 0 and u.hi < v.lo and cap.lo > 0, "endpoint order")
    lw, lz, lcap = log_interval(w), log_interval(z), log_interval(cap)
    lfourpi = log_interval(4/pi)
    ell = 8-4*lw-2*lcap
    Lalpha = log_interval(w*w/z)
    L = 6*lw-2*lz-2
    F = -ell/2-3+L
    c = 4*lfourpi+8*lw-4*lz-2*lcap
    c_from_energy = 4*lfourpi-10-2*F+4*L
    require(max(c.lo, c_from_energy.lo) <= min(c.hi, c_from_energy.hi),
            "energy and endpoint coefficient intervals fail to overlap")
    c16 = 16*c
    target_left = I.decimal('21.66851180520')
    target_right = I.decimal('21.66851180521')
    require(c16.lo > target_left.hi, "strict lower coefficient bound")
    require(c16.hi < target_right.lo, "strict upper coefficient bound")
    shown_left, shown_right = [I.decimal(s) for s in c16.outward_decimal()]
    require(shown_left.hi < c16.lo and c16.hi < shown_right.lo,
            "printed stronger enclosure must be strict")
    centre = Lalpha/8-log_interval(I.rational(2))/4
    # This checks the reported centre as an equilibrium expression only.
    centre_left = I.decimal('-0.080453400358')
    centre_right = I.decimal('-0.080453400357')
    require(centre.lo > centre_left.hi and centre.hi < centre_right.lo,
            "strict centre-expression enclosure")
    quantities = dict(h=h, elliptic_parameter=m, K=K, E=E, pi=pi,
                      u=u, v=v, w=w, z=z, cap=cap,
                      robin_ell=ell, L_alpha=Lalpha, L=L, F=F,
                      c_partial=c, c_partial_from_energy=c_from_energy,
                      sixteen_c_partial=c16, centre_expression=centre)
    receipt = {
        "status": "PASS",
        "arithmetic": "integer outward fixed-point intervals; no floats",
        "scale": str(SCALE),
        "elliptic_terms": ELLIPTIC_TERMS,
        "arctan_terms": ARCTAN_TERMS,
        "log_terms": LOG_TERMS,
        "normalization": {"alpha": "2", "beta": "pi",
                          "endpoint_equations": "u K(k)=2; v E(k)=4; k^2=1-u^2/v^2",
                          "F": "logarithmic interaction minus original potential integral"},
        "root_signs": signs,
        "final_elliptic_tails": tails,
        "quantities": {name: value.record() for name, value in quantities.items()},
        "strict_certified_coefficient_bounds": ["21.66851180520", "21.66851180521"],
        "strict_certified_centre_expression_bounds": ["-0.080453400358", "-0.080453400357"],
        "script_sha256": hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        "scope": "Closed equilibrium coefficient only; no separate kernel leading coefficient."
    }
    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2, sort_keys=True)+'\n', encoding='utf-8')
    print('PASS: 21.66851180520 < 16 c_partial < 21.66851180521')
    print('Outward enclosure:', ' < 16 c_partial < '.join(c16.outward_decimal()))
    print('Certificate written:', args.output.name)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

\section{The complete residual map on the original conductor graph}
\label{sec:GIP}

"""Exact outward certificate; Python integers only, no floating-point input.

Every interval endpoint is an integer divided by SCALE. All divisions round
outward. Explicit analytic tails enclose the infinite defining series.
Run normally and with -O; correctness checks deliberately do not use assert.
"""
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import hashlib
import json

SCALE = 10 ** 70
ELLIPTIC_TERMS = 3200
ARCTAN_TERMS = 128
LOG_TERMS = 256


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise ArithmeticError(message)


def ceil_div(n, d):
    require(d != 0, "zero denominator")
    if d < 0:
        n, d = -n, -d
    return -((-n) // d)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class I:
    lo: int
    hi: int

    def __post_init__(self):
        require(self.lo <= self.hi, "reversed interval")

    @staticmethod
    def rational(n, d=1):
        require(d != 0, "zero rational denominator")
        if d < 0:
            n, d = -n, -d
        return I(n * SCALE // d, ceil_div(n * SCALE, d))

    @staticmethod
    def decimal(s):
        sign = -1 if s.startswith('-') else 1
        s = s.lstrip('+-')
        whole, dot, frac = s.partition('.')
        return I.rational(sign * int(whole + frac), 10 ** len(frac))

    def __add__(self, other):
        other = to_i(other)
        return I(self.lo + other.lo, self.hi + other.hi)

    __radd__ = __add__

    def __neg__(self):
        return I(-self.hi, -self.lo)

    def __sub__(self, other):
        return self + (-to_i(other))

    def __rsub__(self, other):
        return to_i(other) - self

    def __mul__(self, other):
        other = to_i(other)
        values = [a * b for a in (self.lo, self.hi)
                  for b in (other.lo, other.hi)]
        return I(min(values) // SCALE, ceil_div(max(values), SCALE))

    __rmul__ = __mul__

    def __truediv__(self, other):
        other = to_i(other)
        require(other.lo > 0 or other.hi < 0,
                "division interval contains zero")
        pairs = [(a * SCALE, b) for a in (self.lo, self.hi)
                 for b in (other.lo, other.hi)]
        lows = [n // d for n, d in pairs]
        highs = [ceil_div(n, d) for n, d in pairs]
        return I(min(lows), max(highs))

    def __rtruediv__(self, other):
        return to_i(other) / self

    def power(self, n):
        require(isinstance(n, int) and n >= 0, "nonnegative integer power")
        answer, base = I.rational(1), self
        while n:
            if n & 1:
                answer = answer * base
            base = base * base
            n //= 2
        return answer

    def outward_decimal(self, digits=36):
        factor = 10 ** digits
        left = self.lo * factor // SCALE
        right = ceil_div(self.hi * factor, SCALE)

        def display(value):
            sign = '-' if value < 0 else ''
            value = abs(value)
            return sign + str(value // factor) + '.' + str(value % factor).zfill(digits)

        return [display(left), display(right)]

    def record(self):
        return {"scaled_lower": str(self.lo), "scaled_upper": str(self.hi),
                "outward_decimal_36": self.outward_decimal()}


def to_i(value):
    if isinstance(value, I):
        return value
    require(isinstance(value, int), "noninteger scalar")
    return I.rational(value)


def elliptic_bar(m):
    """Enclose 2K(sqrt(m))/pi and 2E(sqrt(m))/pi, retaining m."""
    require(0 < m.lo and m.hi < SCALE, "elliptic parameter outside (0,1)")
    term = I.rational(1)
    ks = I.rational(1)
    es = I.rational(1)
    for n in range(1, ELLIPTIC_TERMS):
        term = term * m * I.rational((2*n-1)**2, 4*n*n)
        ks = ks + term
        es = es - term / (2*n-1)
    n = ELLIPTIC_TERMS
    next_term = term * m * I.rational((2*n-1)**2, 4*n*n)
    ktail = next_term / (1-m)
    etail = ktail / (2*n-1)
    require(0 <= ktail.lo and 0 <= etail.lo, "negative elliptic tail")
    return (ks + I(0, ktail.hi), es - I(0, etail.hi),
            {"K_bar_tail_upper_scaled": str(ktail.hi),
             "E_bar_tail_upper_scaled": str(etail.hi)})


def atan_reciprocal(q):
    x = I.rational(1, q)
    xx = x*x
    term = x
    total = I.rational(0)
    for n in range(ARCTAN_TERMS):
        contribution = term / (2*n+1)
        total = total + contribution if n % 2 == 0 else total - contribution
        term = term * xx
    bound = term / (2*ARCTAN_TERMS+1)
    # The first omitted alternating term has positive sign for the even N.
    return total + I(0, bound.hi)


def log_interval(x):
    require(x.lo > 0, "nonpositive logarithm argument")
    t = (x-1)/(x+1)
    require(-SCALE < t.lo and t.hi < SCALE, "atanh outside unit interval")
    tt = t*t
    term = t
    total = I.rational(0)
    for n in range(LOG_TERMS):
        total = total + 2*term/(2*n+1)
        term = term*tt
    rvalue = max(abs(t.lo), abs(t.hi))
    r = I(rvalue, rvalue)
    bound = 2*r.power(2*LOG_TERMS+1)/((2*LOG_TERMS+1)*(1-r*r))
    return total + I(-bound.hi, bound.hi)

    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path,
                        default=Path(__file__).with_name('CERTIFICATE_RECEIPT.json'))
    args = parser.parse_args()

            "endpoint rationals must be exactly represented")
    signs = {}
    for label, endpoint in [('left', h_left), ('right', h_right)]:
        kb, eb, tail = elliptic_bar(1-endpoint*endpoint)
        residual = 2*endpoint*kb-eb

                        "tails": tail}
        if label == 'left':

    kb, eb, tails = elliptic_bar(m)
    pi = 16*atan_reciprocal(5)-4*atan_reciprocal(239)

    K = pi*kb/2
    E = pi*eb/2
    v = 4/E
    u = h*v

    L = 6*lw-2*lz-2

            "energy and endpoint coefficient intervals fail to overlap")
    c16 = 16*c

## 1. Original quotient and source (OOQ1–2)

The parameters remain
\[
k=4l+1,\quad q=(k+1)^2,\quad q'=(k-7)^2,\quad
d=q-q'=16k-48,\quad n=q/2,\quad \vartheta=\pi/2.
\]
The actual root polynomials are
\[
P_k(y)=i^{-q}\chi_k(c+iy),\quad
P_{k-8}(y)=i^{-q'}\chi_{k-8}(c'+iy),\quad
c=k/2,\quad c'=c-4.
\]
CTV's literal central-root inclusion proves \(P_k=P_{k-8}P_{\partial,k}\), with unchanged roots. The outer polynomial is monic of degree \(d\), each root has modulus at most \(R=k\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2}\), and the target is its original increasing-power remainder frame.

The four source degrees are \(L=d-1,d,q+d-1,q+d\). Their full source is
\[
|P_{k-8}(y)|^2dm_s(y),\qquad
dm_s(y)=\frac{(2\pi)^{s/2}2^{s/2}}{4\pi\Gamma(s/2)}
|\Gamma(s/4+iy/2)|^2dy,\quad s=1,k.
\]
The quotient Gram is the minimum over the actual affine remainder fiber at each \(L\), not merely a matrix having the same determinant. All these norms are strictly positive on nonzero polynomials; the remainder map is onto already at \(L=d-1\), so each target Gram is positive definite.

## 2. Compact equilibrium constants (OOQ3–6)

The rectangle is \(\mathcal K=[3/2,5/2]\times[\pi/4,\pi]\), inside the proved positive EIQ parameter quadrant. The exact equilibrium potential satisfies
\[
V(x)-2P(x)=\ell+D(x),\qquad D\ge0,\qquad D|_{[a,b]}=0.
\]
The support endpoints remain in a compact subset of \((0,\infty)\), with a positive minimum gap, and the densities are uniformly bounded. These follow from the explicit EIQ endpoint and density formulas and their proved parameter smoothness. Thus \(a_*>0\), \(B_*<\infty\), \(b_*>0\), \(M_*<\infty\), and the specified bound \(L_*\) for \(V'\) is finite.

For \(x>0\), the positive logarithmic part gives
\[
P(x)\le\log(1+x)+\log(1+B_*).
\]
The negative part has integral at most
\[
M_*\int_{-1}^1-\log|u|\,du=2M_*,
\]
so \(P(x)\ge-2M_*\). Evaluating the Euler equality on the compact support bounds \(\ell\). For \(x\ge1\) this proves the stated uniform lower estimate
\[
D(x)\ge(\pi/4)\sqrt x-(5/2)\log x-2\log(1+x)-C.
\]
Near zero the compact support is bounded away from zero, so \(P\) is uniformly bounded and \(-\alpha\log x\to+\infty\) uniformly. The tail therefore proves both finiteness of \(C_{\rm tail}\) and integrability defining \(T_*\); on the compact remaining interval \(D\ge0\) suffices. A constant multiple of \((1+x)^2(1+x^{5/2})e^{-\pi\sqrt x/4}\) is an integrable majorant. These constants do not conceal an assumed tail theorem.

The relation defining \(W\) has the correct sign. Integrating the Euler equality gives \(\ell=\int V-2I\), where \(I=\iint\log|x-y|\,d\mu d\mu\), while \(F=I-\int V\). Thus
\[
\ell/2=-F-\tfrac12\int V.
\]
EIQ proves \(P_0=F_\alpha\) and \(\beta\int\sqrt x\,d\mu=2(\alpha+1)\), whence
\[
\int V=2(\alpha+1)-\alpha F_\alpha,\qquad
W=P_0+\ell/2=-F-(\alpha+1)+(1+\alpha/2)F_\alpha.
\]
EIQ parameter smoothness gives bounded first derivatives of \(W\) on \(\mathcal K\), so the explicit \(C_W\) is finite.

## 3. Polynomial evaluation in every direction (OOQ7–8)

Let \(m\ge\max\{1,2/b_*\}\), \(\deg p\le m\), and
\[
M=\max_{[a,b]}|p(x)|e^{-mV(x)/2}.
\]
For nonzero \(p\), choose a maximizing \(x_0\). One of the two sides inside \([a,b]\) has length at least \(1/m\). On that interval \(J\),
\[
|p(x)|\le e^{L_*/2}|p(x_0)|.
\]
The complex-coefficient Chebyshev expansion on the affine copy of \([-1,1]\) has coefficients of modulus at most \(2\|p\|_{\infty,J}\), while \(|T_j'|\le j^2\). Since \(\sum_{j=1}^m j^2\le m^3\), including \(m=1\), the affine derivative factor gives
\[
\|p'\|_{\infty,J}\le4m^3|J|^{-1}\|p\|_{\infty,J}.
\]
Here \(|J|=1/m\). On a one-sided segment of length \([8e^{L_*/2}m^4]^{-1}\), the polynomial consequently differs from \(p(x_0)\) by at most half its modulus. The weight there is at least \(e^{-L_*}e^{-mV(x_0)}\). Integrating proves
\[
\|p\|_{m,V}^2\ge\frac{M^2}{32e^{3L_*/2}m^4},
\quad
M\le C_{\rm BM}m^2\|p\|_{m,V}.
\]

Off the interval, \(\log|p(z)|-mP(z)\) is subharmonic. On its boundary the Euler equality bounds it above by \(\log M+m\ell/2\). In the coordinate \(w=1/z\), its possible singularity at infinity is \((m-\deg p)\log|w|\) plus a harmonic function, hence it extends subharmonically. The maximum principle on the interval complement in the sphere gives the same upper bound everywhere off the interval. Bounded density makes \(P\) continuous at the boundary. The zero polynomial satisfies the resulting inequality directly. Thus
\[
|p(z)|\le C_{\rm BM}m^2e^{m(P(z)+\ell/2)}\|p\|_{m,V}.
\]
For \(|z|\le a_*/2\), each support point obeys
\[
|\log|1-z/t||\le2|z|/a_*,
\]
so \(|P(z)-P_0|\le2|z|/a_*\). This proves OOQ8 with its exact exponent. This lower-lift norm estimate applies to every polynomial, not just a chosen orthogonal direction.

## 4. Quantile polynomial lift (OOQ9–11)

The actual equilibrium's \(n\) consecutive mass-\(1/n\) intervals have total length at most \(B_*\). Their midpoints \(\xi_i\) define
\[
r_n(x)=\prod_{i=1}^n(1-x/\xi_i),\qquad r_n(0)=1.
\]
For \(f_\eta(t)=\log\max\{|x-t|,\eta\}\), the Lipschitz constant is \(1/\eta\). Comparing each midpoint with \(n\) times the integral over its mass interval gives total absolute error at most \(B_*/\eta\). The truncated logarithmic singularity contributes at most \(2nM_*\eta\). With \(\eta=n^{-1/2}\), the sum is \((B_*+2M_*)\sqrt n\). Finally \(\log t\) has Lipschitz constant \(1/a_*\) on the support, giving
\[
\left|\sum_i\log\xi_i-nP_0\right|\le B_*/a_*.
\]
These estimates prove
\[
\log|r_n(x)|\le n(P(x)-P_0)+C_{\rm quant}\sqrt n+C_0.
\]
At a root the left side is minus infinity, so the same inequality holds.

For complex \(|z|\le a_*/2\), the individual inequality
\[
|1-z/\xi_i|\ge1-|z|/a_*\ge e^{-2|z|/a_*}
\]
gives \(|r_n(z)|^{-1}\le e^{2n|z|/a_*}\). This is the needed analytic inverse bound on the complete disk; no zero is moved or ignored.

## 5. Exact remainder and all its coefficient factors (OOQ12–15)

With \(\rho=n^{-1/8}\), \(\widehat P(z)=n^{-d}P_{\partial,k}(nz)\), and \(r_*=R/n\), OOQ13 imposes
\[
n\ge2d+1,\quad n\ge2/b_*,\quad r_*\le\rho/2,\quad
\rho\le\min\{1/2,\sqrt{a_*/2}\},
\]
together with OSP23 and \(k\ge257\). All are eventual for the fixed original quartet, since \(n\asymp k^2\), \(d=O(k)\), and \(r_*=O(k^{-1})\).

For a function holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed disk, the displayed contour formula is a polynomial of degree at most \(d-1\). At any original root of \(\widehat P\), Cauchy's formula returns the function value. The original simple-quartet roots are distinct, so these \(d\) values uniquely determine the remainder; the formula agrees with ordinary division on polynomials.

On the contour, \(|\widehat P(\zeta)|\ge(\rho-r_*)^d\ge(\rho/2)^d\). Expanding the divided difference gives the exact coefficient polynomial
\[
\sum_{a=1}^dp_a\sum_{h=0}^{a-1}\zeta^{a-1-h}z^h.
\]
Because \(\rho\le1\), its coefficient norm is at most \(d\sum_a|p_a|\), and the entire monic product has coefficient sum at most \((1+r_*)^d\). The contour length divided by \(2\pi\) contributes \(\rho\), proving
\[
\|\operatorname{rem}_{\widehat P}f\|_1
\le C_{\rm rem}\max_{|\zeta|=\rho}|f(\zeta)|,\quad
C_{\rm rem}=\rho d(1+r_*)^d(2/\rho)^d.
\]
Its logarithm is \(O(d\log n+\log d)\). Every coefficient of the actual outer root polynomial remains in the map.

## 6. High-degree lower bound (OOQ16–20)

The comparison source is \(|y|^{2Q}e^{-\beta|y|}dy\), with \(Q=q'+\ell_s\), \(\ell_s=(s-1)/4\), and \(\beta=\vartheta\pm1/q\). Let
\[
\alpha_0=(Q-\tfrac12)/n,\qquad
c_{\rm high}=(2Q+1)\log n-2nW(\alpha_0,\beta).
\]
At \(L=q+d-1\), the two parity degrees are both \(n+d/2-1\). At \(L=q+d\), they are \(n+d/2\) and \(n+d/2-1\). In particular \(n\le m_e,m_o\le n+d\).

The exact parity parameters are
\[
(\alpha_e,\beta_e)=((Q-\tfrac12)/m_e,n\beta/m_e),\quad
(\alpha_o,\beta_o)=((Q+\tfrac12)/m_o,n\beta/m_o).
\]
The inequalities \(d/q<1/16\), \(\ell_s/q<1/64\), and the actual rounding prove that these and \((\alpha_0,\beta)\) lie in \(\mathcal K\). For example the alpha parameters lie above \(5/3-8/(9q)>3/2\) and below \(2+1/32+1/q<5/2\); using \(1/q<\pi/8\) gives rates between \(\pi/3\) and \(5\pi/8\), inside the retained rectangle.

Writing \(p(nz)=p_e(z^2)+zp_o(z^2)\), cancellation of the odd cross terms between \(z=\sqrt x\) and \(z=-\sqrt x\) gives exactly
\[
n^{-(2Q+1)}\|p\|_{\exp}^2
=\int|p_e(x)|^2x^{Q-1/2}e^{-n\beta\sqrt x}dx
+\int|p_o(x)|^2x^{Q+1/2}e^{-n\beta\sqrt x}dx.
\]
Each half-axis contributes \(1/(2\sqrt x)\), so no factor two is absent.

For either parity, \(|m-n|\le d+1\),
\[
m|\alpha-\alpha_0|\le1+(5/2)|m-n|,\qquad
m|\beta_m-\beta|\le\pi|m-n|.
\]
The mean-value formula on the rectangle, together with the specified \(C_W\), proves
\[
|mW(\alpha,\beta_m)-nW(\alpha_0,\beta)|\le C_W(d+2).
\]
Applying OOQ8 at \(x=\zeta^2\), then \(|\zeta|=\rho\le1\), Cauchy–Schwarz in the two parity norms, and the remainder bound yields
\[
\|v\|_2\le C_{\rm rem}\sqrt2C_{\rm BM}(n+d)^2
e^{nW+C_W(d+2)+2(n+d)\rho^2/a_*}
n^{-(2Q+1)/2}\|p\|_{\exp}.
\]
This holds for every lift with remainder \(v\). Squaring and rearranging gives the lower target-form bound with exactly \(E_{\rm high}^-\) in OOQ24.

## 7. High-degree upper bound and coordinate transport (OOQ21–25)

For a prescribed degree-less-than-\(d\) remainder \(v(z)\), form the actual analytic remainder
\[
a_v=\operatorname{rem}_{\widehat P}\bigl(v/r_n(z^2)\bigr),\qquad
p_v(nz)=r_n(z^2)a_v(z).
\]
The denominator has no zero in the disk because its squared-coordinate roots are at least \(a_*>\rho^2\). This polynomial has degree at most \(2n+d-1=q+d-1\), admitted at both high endpoints. Its values at all actual outer roots equal \(v\), so it is an actual lift.

On the contour, \(|v(\zeta)|\le\sqrt d\|v\|_2\), and OOQ11 gives
\[
\|a_v\|_1\le C_{\rm rem}\sqrt d\,e^{2n\rho^2/a_*}\|v\|_2.
\]
On either real half-axis,
\[
|a_v(\pm\sqrt x)|\le\|a_v\|_1(1+\sqrt x)^{d-1}.
\]
The definition of \(C_{\rm tail}\) implies
\[
(1+\sqrt x)^{2(d-1)}
\le e^{2C_{\rm tail}(d-1)}e^{2(d-1)D(x)}.
\]
The quantile bound and \(2P-V=-\ell-D\) then leave
\[
e^{-2nP_0-n\ell}\,e^{-[n-2(d-1)]D(x)}
=e^{-2nW}\,e^{-[n-2(d-1)]D(x)}.
\]
Since \(n-2(d-1)\ge1\), integration is bounded by \(T_*\). The exact \(y=nz\) Jacobian/power factor is \(n^{2Q+1}\), giving OOQ23 and precisely \(E_{\rm high}^+\).

If \(w\) is the original \(y\)-remainder coefficient vector, its scaled vector is
\[
v=D_nw,\qquad D_n=\operatorname{diag}(1,n,\ldots,n^{d-1}).
\]
Indeed division after the literal substitution has remainder \(v(z)=\sum w_jn^jz^j\). Therefore
\[
Q_{\rm original}=D_n^*Q_{\rm scaled}D_n,\qquad
I\preceq D_n^*D_n\preceq n^{2(d-1)}I.
\]
Adding \(2(d-1)\log n\) to the maximum of the two scalar errors proves OOQ25 in the original frame. Since \(n\rho^2=n^{3/4}\), \(\sqrt n\le n^{3/4}\), and \(\log C_{\rm rem}=O(d\log n)\), the high error is \(O(n^{3/4}+d\log n)\).

## 8. Low degrees and the complete additional ideal column (OOQ26–29)

Let \(y_0=2Q/\beta\) and \(g(Q,\beta)=2Q\log(2Q/\beta)-2Q\). On \([y_0,y_0+1]\), the weight is at least \(e^{g(Q,\beta)-\beta}\).

On \([0,1]\), the orthonormal shifted Legendre polynomial of degree \(j\) has coefficient sum at most \(\sqrt{2j+1}\,8^j\): Rodrigues' coefficients are \((-1)^{j-r}\binom jr\binom{j+r}r\), whose absolute sum is at most \(2^j4^j\). The Euclidean operator norm of their complete coefficient matrix is therefore at most
\[
\sqrt{(d+1)(2d+1)}\,8^d.
\]
The translation of coefficient vectors by \(-y_0\) has norm at most \(\sqrt{d+1}(1+y_0)^d\). Multiplying these two bounds, and then squaring, proves the lower Gram denominator
\[
(d+1)^2(2d+1)64^d(1+y_0)^{2d}
\]
in OOQ26. It is a form bound on every coefficient vector.

The upper form bound is the trace, exactly
\[
\sum_{j=0}^d2(2Q+2j)!/\beta^{2Q+2j+1}.
\]
At \(L=d-1\) the remainder map is the identity. At \(L=d\) it is exactly \([I_d,-p_{\rm low}]\), with every lower coefficient of \(P_{\partial,k}\). Its norm squared is \(1+\|p_{\rm low}\|_2^2\), bounded by \((d+1)(1+R)^{2d}\). For any lift \(w\) of \(v\), \(\|w\|_2\ge\|v\|_2/\|[I,-p_{\rm low}]\|_2\). Thus the extra factor contributes precisely one further \(\log(d+1)\) and \(2d\log(1+R)\) to the lower-error exponent, as in OOQ28. The canonical lift \((v,0)\) proves the upper quotient bound.

The integral estimates
\[
m\log m-m+1\le\log(m!)\le m\log m-m+1+\log m
\]
show that each trace summand's logarithm exceeds \(g(Q,\beta)\) by at most \(O(d\log(Q+d)+\log(Q+d))\). Summing adds only \(\log(d+1)\). The lower displayed error has that same order, because \(Q\asymp q\), \(d=O(k)\), \(R=O_{\delta,\gamma}(k)\), and the rates remain in a fixed positive interval. This proves both OOQ29 and \(E_{\rm low}=O_{\delta,\gamma}(d\log q)\).

## 9. Complete original source transport and finite error (OOQ30–35)

OSP20–26 is a full polynomial-form comparison between the actual \(P_{k-8}\) multiplier and \(y^{q'}\), preserving the original source order and every root coefficient. Its error is \(\mathcal E_k\). OFV5–7 is the literal recurrence
\[

t_a=2a+\tfrac12,\quad
\beta_s=(2\pi)^{s/2}/(\sqrt2\,\Gamma(s/2)),
\]
and the full-form comparison to the \(y^{2\ell_s}\) multiplier has lower ratio one and upper ratio \(e^{r_{\ell_s}}\). The proof includes the inner interval and every multiplier factor. For \(s=1\), \(\beta_1=1\), \(\ell_1=0\), and \(r_0=0\).

The pointwise one-factor Gamma inequalities are
\[
L_he^{-(\vartheta+h)|y|}\le d\sigma/dy
\le U_he^{-(\vartheta-h)|y|},\qquad h=1/q.
\]
Composing the three complete inequalities gives OOQ31 with exactly the lower scalar \(\beta_sL_he^{-\mathcal E_k}\), upper scalar \(\beta_sU_he^{\mathcal E_k+r_{\ell_s}}\), and exponent \(Q_s=q'+\ell_s\). The degree condition holds because \(L\le q+d\le2q\). Each comparison is on the same coefficient polynomial and the same actual remainder fiber; taking the attained minima therefore proves the quotient comparison without an invariant-kernel premise.

The common centers are
\[
c_{\rm lo}=g(q,\vartheta),\qquad
c_{\rm hi}=2q\log(q/2)-qW(2,\vartheta).
\]
The finite error OOQ33 includes both previously proved errors, the full logarithms of \(L_h,U_h\), \(\mathcal E_k\), \(r_{\ell_s}\), and the absolute discrepancies from these two common centers. Thus each scalar comparison is bounded in both directions by the common \(\varepsilon_k\), while the complete \(\beta_s\) remains outside it. This proves OOQ34 simultaneously for both source orders.

For the size estimate, \(\mathcal E_k=O_{\delta,\gamma}(1)\), \(r_{\ell_s}=O(1/k)\), and the sine constants have logarithmic cost \(O(\log q)\). Also \(Q_s-q=-d+\ell_s=O(k)\) and \(|\beta-\vartheta|=1/q\). The derivatives of \(g\) and the bounded derivatives of \(W\) consequently give both scalar discrepancies \(O(k\log q+\log q)\). For the high expression the difference of the logarithmic prefactors is \((2Q_s+1-2q)\log n\), and the \(W\) discrepancy multiplied by \(2n=q\) is \(O(k+1)\). All terms therefore give
\[
\varepsilon_k=O_{\delta,\gamma}(q^{3/4}+k\log q)=o(q).
