idempotent and projects onto the orthogonal complement of the entire
$S_NU_N^{-1}(K)$. Thus its Gram is the minimum norm of the transported
quotient ROQ23. Replacing $Y_{L,N}$ by another source lift of $L$ adds
columns in $I_N$, which this projector kills. Replacing the section
$L$ by another section of ROQ6 adds columns in $K$; their lifts lie
in the span of $J_N$ and are killed. Therefore ROQ25 computes
the specified quotient metric independently of either choice.

Before applying $S_N$, the same projection gives
\[
 Q_{\Xi,N}
 =L^*G_NL-L^*G_NI_K(I_K^*G_NI_K)^{-1}I_K^*G_NL.
 \tag{ROQ26}
\]
To prove it, $Y_{L,N}$ and $Y_{K,N}$ are perpendicular to the ideal,
so projection off $J_N$ only subtracts
$Y_{K,N}(Y_{K,N}^*Y_{K,N})^{-1}Y_{K,N}^*Y_{L,N}$.
Using $U_NU_N^*=R_N$ in their Gram products yields exactly ROQ26.
It is also the minimum of the original $G_N$ norm on $Ly+K$, so
it agrees with the already proved ROQ11 and ROQ16.

The all-rank exterior estimate CEP33--35 applies to ROQ23: represent
a quotient class by its minimum lift in the denominator's orthogonal
complement, apply $S_N$, then project off the target denominator.
This projection has every exterior norm at most one. Consequently the
induced $j$th exterior norm is at most $\|\bigwedge^jS_N\|$, and its
inverse is at most $\|\bigwedge^jS_N^{-1}\|$ by the identical argument
for $S_N^{-1}$. CEP34 bounds both logarithms from above by $E_N$.
Applying them to the fixed frame ROQ6 and squaring exterior volumes gives
\[
 \left|\log\det\widetilde Q_{\Xi,N}
                -\log\det Q_{\Xi,N}\right|\le2E_N,\qquad
 \left|\sum_{N\in\mathcal N}\sigma_N\log\det\widetilde Q_{\Xi,N}
                       -F_{\Xi,k}^{(s)}\right|
                       \le\epsilon_{A,k}^{(s)}=o(kq).
 \tag{ROQ27}
\]
All cross terms in $J_N^*S_N^*S_NJ_N$ remain present in ROQ25,
including $P_{<v}(\chi_k S^a)$ and its pairings with the minimum
kernel lifts. Its ideal columns can equally be generated from the full
products $d_{rs}$ and maps $\mathcal U_{A,L}$ in CEP41--45, because
those formulas prove exactly $S_NZ_N^{\chi}$ column by column.
This supplies the typed relation between the explicit residual
observation and the conductor graph at all four original cutoffs.

% Full original-root comparison; no sealed provider is modified.
\section{A quantitative power comparison for the actual outer-strip quotient}
\label{sec:OSP}

Retain the original real parameters and integers
\[
0<\delta<\tfrac12,\quad \gamma>2,\quad k=4l+1\ge9,\quad
q=(k+1)^2,\quad k'=k-8,\quad q'=(k-7)^2,\quad
\Delta=q-q'=16k-48.
\tag{OSP1}
\]
The two source orders in every formula below are precisely $s=1,k$.
Set $b=s/2$, $M_s=(2\pi)^{s/2}$, and retain the full original measure
\[
dm_s(y)=M_s\frac{2^b}{4\pi\Gamma(b)}
       |\Gamma(b/2+iy/2)|^2\,dy.
\tag{OSP2}
\]
In the original coordinate $S=k/2+iy$, and respectively
$S'=k/2-4+iy$, the complete monic root polynomials are
\[
\begin{split}
P_k(y)&=i^{-q}\chi_k(k/2+iy)
 =\prod_{a,b_0=0}^{k}
 [y-(2b_0-k)\gamma+i(2a-k)\delta],\\
P_{k'}(y)&=i^{-q'}\chi_{k'}(k/2-4+iy)
 =\prod_{a,b_0=0}^{k'}
 [y-(2b_0-k')\gamma+i(2a-k')\delta].
\end{split}\tag{OSP3}
\]
The index $b_0$ in these products is distinct from the source parameter
$b=s/2$. Each root occurs with exactly its displayed multiplicity.
The map $(a,b_0)\mapsto(a+4,b_0+4)$ identifies the second root list
with the central subrectangle of the first, so
\[
P_k=P_{k'}P_{\partial,k},\qquad
P_{\partial,k}(y)=
\prod_{(a,b_0)\in\{0,\ldots,k\}^2\setminus\{4,\ldots,k-4\}^2}
[y-(2b_0-k)\gamma+i(2a-k)\delta].
\tag{OSP4}
\]
This proves the factorization and its monic constant; the outer degree
is $\Delta$. Both complete root lists are invariant under
$\omega\mapsto-\omega$. Every root has modulus at most
\[
R=k\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2}.
\tag{OSP5}
\]

\subsection{The two original source masses and a proved interval lower bound}

We first record the source facts needed in the comparison, including
their constants and proofs. For $a>0$ and real $x$, the two Euler
integrals and the change of variables in the beta integral give
\[
\frac{\Gamma(a+ix)\Gamma(a-ix)}{\Gamma(2a)}
 =\int_{\mathbb R}e^{ixu}(2\cosh(u/2))^{-2a}\,du.
\tag{OSP6}
\]
For example the intermediate beta integral is
$\int_0^\infty t^{a+ix-1}(1+t)^{-2a}dt$, and $t=e^u$
gives the displayed expression. Absolute convergence follows from
$a>0$. Rotating Euler's integral through
$\operatorname{sgn}(y)\theta$, $0<\theta<\pi/2$, gives
\[
|\Gamma(a+iy/2)|
 \le e^{-\theta|y|/2}\Gamma(a)(\cos\theta)^{-a}.
\tag{OSP7}
\]
The rotation follows from Cauchy's theorem on the intervening
sector: the large circular arc tends to zero because its real
exponential has positive cosine, and the small one tends to zero
because $a>0$. The remaining radial integral has absolute value
at most $\Gamma(a)(\cos\theta)^{-a}$. In particular the Fourier
transform in OSP6 is integrable. Fourier inversion, followed by
$y=2x$, now gives
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}e^{i\xi y}\,dm_s(y)
  =M_s(\cosh\xi)^{-b},\qquad
\int_{\mathbb R}dm_s=M_s.
\tag{OSP8}
\]
The same identity holds analytically for $|\operatorname{Im}\xi|<\pi/2$:
OSP7 with any larger $\theta<\pi/2$ supplies an integrable dominating
function on each smaller strip. Substituting $\xi=-it$ proves
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}e^{ty}\,dm_s(y)=M_s(\cos t)^{-b},
\qquad |t|<\pi/2.
\tag{OSP9}
\]
This also proves finiteness of all moments used below.

Write
\[
d\sigma(y)=\frac{|\Gamma(1/4+iy/2)|^2}{2\pi}\,dy,\quad
C_L=\frac{\pi}{\Gamma(3/4)^2},\quad
\ell_s=\frac{s-1}{4},\quad
\beta_s=\frac{M_s}{\sqrt2\,\Gamma(s/2)}.
\tag{OSP10}
\]
The two values of $\ell_s$ are the integers $0,l$. The reflection
identity gives a useful explicit lower bound
\[
\frac{d\sigma}{dy}(y)\ge C_Le^{-\pi|y|}.
\tag{OSP11}
\]
Here is its proof on the required domain. For $0<\operatorname{Re}z<1$
the Euler integrals give
$\Gamma(z)\Gamma(1-z)=\int_0^\infty t^{z-1}/(1+t)\,dt$.
On a keyhole contour with argument in $(0,2\pi)$, the circular
terms vanish with bounds $O(r^{\operatorname{Re}z})$ at zero
and $O(R^{\operatorname{Re}z-1})$ at infinity. The residue at $-1$
is $e^{i\pi(z-1)}$; the two radial integrals therefore give
$(1-e^{2\pi iz})\int_0^\infty t^{z-1}/(1+t)\,dt
=2\pi i e^{i\pi(z-1)}$. Their ratio is $\pi/\sin(\pi z)$.
At $z=1/4+iy/2$ this proves
\[
|\Gamma(1/4+iy/2)|^2|\Gamma(3/4-iy/2)|^2
 =\frac{2\pi^2}{\cosh(\pi y)}.
\]
The unrotated Euler integral bounds the second squared factor by
$\Gamma(3/4)^2$, proving
$d\sigma/dy\ge C_L/\cosh(\pi y)\ge C_Le^{-\pi|y|}$.

Gamma recurrence, proved by one integration by parts in Euler's
integral, gives the exact original-source identity
\[
dm_s(y)=\beta_s
 \prod_{j=0}^{\ell_s-1}\bigl(y^2+(2j+\tfrac12)^2\bigr)\,d\sigma(y).
\tag{OSP12}
\]
Indeed $b/2=\ell_s+1/4$, and each recurrence factor before
squaring and clearing denominators is
$j+1/4+iy/2$; its squared modulus is
$[y^2+(2j+1/2)^2]/4$. The factor $4^{-\ell_s}$ together with
the prefactor in OSP2 is exactly $\beta_s/(2\pi)$, because
$b=2\ell_s+1/2$. This proves every factor in OSP12.
For $s=1$ its product is empty and $\beta_1=1$.
In particular, on the full interval $q\le y\le2q$,
\[
\frac{dm_s}{dy}(y)
 \ge \beta_s q^{2\ell_s}C_Le^{-2\pi q}.
\tag{OSP13}
\]
The source mass-to-lower-density factor obeys the uniform finite bound
\[
\frac{M_s}{\beta_s q^{2\ell_s}}
 =\sqrt2\,\Gamma(b)q^{-2\ell_s}
 \le\sqrt{2\pi}\qquad(s=1,k).
\tag{OSP14}
\]
To prove the inequality, use
$\Gamma(b)=\sqrt\pi\prod_{j=0}^{2\ell_s-1}(j+1/2)
\le\sqrt\pi\,b^{2\ell_s}$ and $b\le q$.
All source masses have thus been retained before taking this exact
ratio.

\subsection{A complete coefficient-space estimate for the inner interval}

Let $p\in\mathbb C[y]$ have degree at most $d$, and let
$0<T\le q/2$. Then
\[
\sup_{|y|\le T}|p(y)|^2
 \le \frac{(d+1)^2\,10^{2d}}q
                  \int_q^{2q}|p(u)|^2\,du.
\tag{OSP15}
\]
This controls every coefficient direction; no assumption on zeros,
leading coefficient, or extremizers of $p$ is made.

For proof define the Legendre polynomial
$L_j(x)=(2^j j!)^{-1}(d/dx)^j(x^2-1)^j$.
Its leading coefficient is $(2j)!/[2^j(j!)^2]$. Integrating by
parts $j$ times, with all lower boundary derivatives zero, proves
orthogonality to lower powers and
\[
\int_{-1}^1L_j(x)^2\,dx
=\frac{(2j)!}{2^{2j}(j!)^2}\int_{-1}^1(1-x^2)^j\,dx
=\frac2{2j+1}.
\]
For the middle integral set $x=2t-1$; repeated integration by parts
gives $\int_0^1t^j(1-t)^jdt=(j!)^2/(2j+1)!$.
Consequently $\sqrt{2j+1}L_j(2z-3)$, $0\le j\le d$,
form an orthonormal basis for degree-at-most-$d$ polynomials on
$[1,2]$. Leibniz's rule also gives the explicit identity
\[
L_j(x)=2^{-j}\sum_{h=0}^j\binom jh^2
                         (x-1)^{j-h}(x+1)^h.
\]
For $|x|\le4$ its modulus is at most
$(5/2)^j\sum_h\binom jh^2\le(5/2)^j4^j=10^j$;
the sum inequality follows by comparing with
$(\sum_h\binom jh)^2=4^j$.
Expanding $p(qz)$ in the displayed orthonormal basis and applying
Cauchy--Schwarz gives, for $|z|\le T/q\le1/2$,
\[
|p(qz)|^2
\le\sum_{j=0}^d(2j+1)10^{2j}
                  \int_1^2|p(qv)|^2\,dv
\le(d+1)^2\,10^{2d}\int_1^2|p(qv)|^2\,dv .
\]
Here $|2z-3|\le4$ and $\sum_{j=0}^d(2j+1)=(d+1)^2$.
Changing variables proves OSP15, including $d=0$.

\subsection{The exact original-root map and a finite full-norm comparison}

In this subsection $P$ is either of the complete polynomials
$P_k,P_{k'}$ in OSP3, and $Q=\deg P$ is respectively $q,q'$.
For $d\ge0$ retain the two injections into the same original
polynomial Hilbert space
\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal J_P:\mathbb C[y]_{\le d}&\longrightarrow
          \mathbb C[y]_{\le Q+d},&p&\longmapsto Pp,\\
\mathcal J_{0,Q}:\mathbb C[y]_{\le d}&\longrightarrow
          \mathbb C[y]_{\le Q+d},&p&\longmapsto y^Qp .
\end{split}\tag{OSP16}
\]
Their codomain norm is precisely $m_s$ in OSP2.
If $P(y)=\sum_{a=0}^QP_a y^a$, set $P_a=0$ outside this range.
In increasing coefficient frames their matrices are
\[
(\mathsf J_P)_{rj}=P_{r-j},\qquad
(\mathsf J_{0,Q})_{rj}=\mathbf1_{\{r=Q+j\}},
\quad 0\le r\le Q+d,\quad 0\le j\le d.
\tag{OSP17}
\]
Thus the exact isomorphism between their images is
$y^Qp\mapsto Pp$, with inverse $Pp\mapsto y^Qp$.
It preserves the original coefficient vector $p$. The first
matrix contains every actual root coefficient; none is replaced
inside that map. Returning to $S$ or $S'$ multiplies the relevant
relation columns by the actual phase $i^Q$ and applies the
triangular coordinate pullback with diagonal entries $i^j$.
Each has the stated exact inverse and determinant of modulus one.

Suppose
\[
R<T\le q/2.
\tag{OSP18}
\]
Define the finite positive constants
\[
\begin{split}
\eta_{Q,T}&=\frac{Q R^2}{T^2-R^2},\\
\kappa_{Q,d,T,s}
 &=\frac{M_s}{\beta_s q^{2\ell_s}C_L}
    \frac{(d+1)^2}{q}\,
    e^{2\pi q}\,10^{2d}
             \left(\frac{T^2+R^2}{q^2}\right)^Q,\\
e_{Q,d,T,s}&=\eta_{Q,T}+\log(1+\kappa_{Q,d,T,s}).
\end{split}\tag{OSP19}
\]
Then every $p\in\mathbb C[y]_{\le d}$ satisfies
\[
e^{-e_{Q,d,T,s}}\int_{\mathbb R}|y|^{2Q}|p(y)|^2\,dm_s(y)
\le\int_{\mathbb R}|P(y)p(y)|^2\,dm_s(y)
\le e^{e_{Q,d,T,s}}
      \int_{\mathbb R}|y|^{2Q}|p(y)|^2\,dm_s(y).
\tag{OSP20}
\]

Here is a proof retaining the entire inner region. Pair the actual
roots as $\omega,-\omega$. On $|y|\ge T$, each paired quotient is
$1-\omega^2/y^2$, so
\[
\left|\log\frac{|P(y)|^2}{|y|^{2Q}}\right|
\le -Q\log(1-R^2/T^2)
\le\frac{Q R^2}{T^2-R^2}=\eta_{Q,T}.
\tag{OSP21}
\]
The first inequality uses $1-u\le|1-z|\le1+u$ for $|z|\le u<1$
on each of $Q/2$ pairs. The second follows by integrating
$1/(1-u)\le1/(1-u_0)$ on $0\le u\le u_0=R^2/T^2$.
For every real $y$, the same pairing gives
$|P(y)|^2\le(y^2+R^2)^Q$. Write
\[
A_B=\int_q^{2q}|y|^{2Q}|p(y)|^2\,dm_s(y).
\]
For nonzero $p$ this number is positive, and OSP13 gives
$A_B\ge q^{2Q}\beta_s q^{2\ell_s}C_Le^{-2\pi q}
 \int_q^{2q}|p(y)|^2dy$.
OSP15 and the exact full mass OSP8 imply
\[
\begin{split}
\int_{|y|<T}|P(y)p(y)|^2\,dm_s(y)
 &\le M_s(T^2+R^2)^Q\sup_{|y|\le T}|p(y)|^2
 \le\kappa_{Q,d,T,s}A_B,\\
\int_{|y|<T}|y|^{2Q}|p(y)|^2\,dm_s(y)
 &\le M_sT^{2Q}\sup_{|y|\le T}|p(y)|^2
 \le\kappa_{Q,d,T,s}A_B .
\end{split}\tag{OSP22}
\]
Let $A_{\rm out}$ and $B_{\rm out}$ be the integrals outside
$(-T,T)$ with factors $|y|^{2Q}$ and $|P|^2$, respectively.
Since $[q,2q]$ is outside that interval, $A_B\le A_{\rm out}$.
OSP21 gives
$e^{-\eta}A_{\rm out}\le B_{\rm out}\le e^\eta A_{\rm out}$.
OSP22 bounds both inner contributions by $\kappa A_{\rm out}$.
Therefore the full reference norm is at most
$(1+\kappa)A_{\rm out}$ and at least $A_{\rm out}$, while the
full actual norm is at least $e^{-\eta}A_{\rm out}$ and at most
$(e^\eta+\kappa)A_{\rm out}\le e^\eta(1+\kappa)A_{\rm out}$.
These four inequalities prove OSP20. The zero polynomial satisfies
it directly.

\subsection{Uniform bounded logarithmic cost at every required dimension}

Choose the fixed number and cutoff
\[
\epsilon=2^{-32},\qquad T=\epsilon q,
\]
and impose the explicit finite conditions
\[
k\ge29,\qquad
k\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2}\le\frac{\epsilon q}{2}.
\tag{OSP23}
\]
In particular $T\ge2R$, as required for a uniform margin in OSP21.
These conditions hold eventually for every fixed original
$\delta,\gamma$; the sufficient bound
$k\ge\max\{29,2\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2}/\epsilon\}$
follows from $q\ge k^2$. The first condition implies $q'\ge q/2$:
$2(k-7)^2-(k+1)^2=k^2-30k+97$ is positive at $k=29$
and is increasing thereafter.

For $Q\in\{q',q\}$ and every $0\le d\le2q$, set
\[
\begin{split}
K_q&=\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{C_L}\frac{(2q+1)^2}{q}e^{-2q},\\
\mathcal E_k&=\frac{qR^2}{\epsilon^2q^2-R^2}+\log(1+K_q).
\end{split}\tag{OSP24}
\]
Then OSP19 satisfies $e_{Q,d,T,s}\le\mathcal E_k$ for both
original source orders. To verify this uniformly, OSP14,
$T^2+R^2\le(5/4)\epsilon^2q^2$, $Q\ge q/2$ and $d\le2q$
give
\[
\kappa_{Q,d,T,s}
\le\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}}{C_L}\frac{(2q+1)^2}{q}
\exp\left(q\{2\pi+4\log10+\tfrac12\log(5/4)+\log\epsilon\}\right).
\tag{OSP25}
\]
The expression in braces is less than $-2$. Indeed
$\pi<4$, $\log10<4\log2$, $\log(5/4)<1/4$, and
$\log2>2/3$ give an upper bound
$8-16\log2+1/8<-61/24<-2$.
For completeness, $\pi<4$ follows from
$\pi/4=\int_0^1(1+x^2)^{-1}dx<1$; and the substitution
$x=(1+t)/(1-t)$ in $\log2=\int_1^2dx/x$ gives
$\log2=2\int_0^{1/3}(1-t^2)^{-1}dt>2/3$.
The logarithm bound follows by integrating $1/(1+x)<1$.
This proves OSP25 with $K_q$ as stated. Also
\[
0\le\mathcal E_k
\le \frac{4(\delta^2+\gamma^2)}{3\epsilon^2}+\log(1+K_q).
\tag{OSP26}
\]
Here $R^2\le\epsilon^2q^2/4$ and $R^2/q\le\delta^2+\gamma^2$.
Thus the logarithmic norm cost is bounded at fixed original
parameters, uniformly over all these coefficient degrees and both
unchanged source orders.

\subsection{Every relation determinant and the exact outer quotient}

For a nonzero polynomial $P$ and $a\ge0$ define in the unchanged monomial frame
\[
\begin{split}
D_a(P;s)&=\det\left[\int_{\mathbb R}y^{i+j}|P(y)|^2\,dm_s(y)
                                      \right]_{0\le i,j<a},\\
\mathcal D_a(Q;s)&=\det\left[\int_{\mathbb R}y^{2Q+i+j}\,dm_s(y)
                                      \right]_{0\le i,j<a},
\qquad D_0=\mathcal D_0=1 .
\end{split}\tag{OSP27}
\]
All nonempty Grams are positive definite, because a nonzero
polynomial has positive squared modulus on an open subinterval
of the strictly positive original measure. In the notation of
OSP17 their exact matrices are
$\mathsf J_P^*H^{(s)}_{Q+a-1}\mathsf J_P$ and
$\mathsf J_{0,Q}^*H^{(s)}_{Q+a-1}\mathsf J_{0,Q}$,
where $H^{(s)}_{Q+a-1}$ is the complete original moment Gram.
Consequently OSP20--26 prove for $1\le a\le2q+1$
\[
\left|\log D_a(P;s)-\log\mathcal D_a(Q;s)\right|
\le a\mathcal E_k,\qquad P=P_k\ \hbox{or}\ P_{k'} .
\tag{OSP28}
\]
To see the determinant step exactly, conjugate the actual Gram by
the inverse positive square root of the reference Gram. OSP20
places every eigenvalue of the resulting positive Hermitian
matrix in $[e^{-\mathcal E_k},e^{\mathcal E_k}]$. The logarithm
of its determinant is the sum of its $a$ eigenvalue logarithms,
proving OSP28. This is the full exterior determinant estimate,
including every polynomial coefficient direction. The estimate
also holds at $a=0$ with both sides zero.

For $t\in\{0,1,q,q+1\}$, let $L=t+\Delta-1$. The actual quotient
has source $\mathbb C[y]_{\le L}$ in measure
$|P_{k'}(y)|^2dm_s(y)$, target the increasing remainder frame of
$\mathbb C[y]/(P_{\partial,k})$, and its minimum Gram
$Q_{\partial,L}^{(s)}$. Define a comparison quotient with source
$\mathbb C[y]_{\le L}$ in measure $|y|^{2q'}dm_s(y)$, target the
increasing remainder frame of $\mathbb C[y]/(y^\Delta)$, and
minimum Gram $Q_{0,L}^{(s)}$. Its source measure still has order
$s$ and the full mass factor in OSP2.

For precision, the exact map relating the coefficient presentations
is the degree-preserving isomorphism
\[
\mathcal U_L(y^j)=
\begin{cases}
y^j,&0\le j<\Delta,\\
P_{\partial,k}(y)y^{j-\Delta},&\Delta\le j\le L.
\end{cases}\tag{OSP29}
\]
Its coefficient matrix has diagonal entries one and no terms of
degree greater than that of its input column. It is therefore
invertible with determinant one. If $\mathsf R_{\partial,L}$
is division remainder modulo $P_{\partial,k}$ and
$\mathsf R_{0,L}$ is division remainder modulo $y^\Delta$,
then
$\mathsf R_{\partial,L}\mathcal U_L=\mathsf R_{0,L}$:
the first $\Delta$ basis vectors map to their stated remainders,
and every later vector maps into the actual ideal. This proves
the precise morphism between the quotient coefficient spaces;
no equality of their metrics is assumed.

Using the original monic relation frames on the two sources gives
the exact identities
\[
\det Q_{\partial,t+\Delta-1}^{(s)}
 =\frac{D_{t+\Delta}(P_{k'};s)}{D_t(P_k;s)},\qquad
\det Q_{0,t+\Delta-1}^{(s)}
 =\frac{\mathcal D_{t+\Delta}(q';s)}{\mathcal D_t(q;s)} .
\tag{OSP30}
\]
For proof, append to $1,y,\ldots,y^{\Delta-1}$ the ideal frame
$P_{\partial,k},yP_{\partial,k},\ldots,y^{t-1}P_{\partial,k}$.
Its source coefficient determinant is one by OSP29. The relation
Gram is $D_t(P_k;s)$ because $P_{k'}P_{\partial,k}=P_k$.
Completing the square in the ideal coordinates gives the minimum
quotient Gram as the Schur complement; the determinant of the
full source Gram is the product of that determinant and the
relation determinant. This proves the first identity.
For the second repeat the same calculation with $y^\Delta$:
$y^{q'}y^\Delta=y^q$, with the original source order $s$.
The same proof includes $t=0$ using the empty relation block.

OSP28 applies to every index here, since
$t+\Delta\le q+\Delta+1\le2q+1$. Define the exact endpoint
difference $\varepsilon_t^{(s)}$ by
\[
\log\det Q_{\partial,t+\Delta-1}^{(s)}
=\log\mathcal D_{t+\Delta}(q';s)-\log\mathcal D_t(q;s)
 +\varepsilon_t^{(s)} .
\]
Then, separately at each of the four endpoints,
\[
|\varepsilon_t^{(s)}|\le(2t+\Delta)\mathcal E_k.
\tag{OSP31}
\]
In particular set
\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal F_{0,k}^{(s)}
={}&\log\mathcal D_\Delta(q';s)
    +\log\mathcal D_{\Delta+1}(q';s)
    -\log\mathcal D_{q+\Delta}(q';s)
    -\log\mathcal D_{q+\Delta+1}(q';s)\\
 &-\log\mathcal D_1(q;s)
    +\log\mathcal D_q(q;s)+\log\mathcal D_{q+1}(q;s).
\end{split}\tag{OSP32}
\]
The actual four-endpoint quantity of CTV13 therefore obeys the
proved finite estimate
\[
\boxed{\displaystyle
\left|\mathcal F_{\partial,k}^{(s)}-\mathcal F_{0,k}^{(s)}\right|
\le4(q+\Delta+1)\mathcal E_k
=O_{\delta,\gamma}(q)=o(kq),\qquad s=1,k .}
\tag{OSP33}
\]
Indeed its exact error is
$\varepsilon_0+\varepsilon_1-\varepsilon_q-\varepsilon_{q+1}$;
summing OSP31 gives
$\Delta+(\Delta+2)+(2q+\Delta)+(2q+\Delta+2)
=4(q+\Delta+1)$. OSP26 and $\Delta<q$ prove the last two
estimates. This calculation uses all four source degrees
$\Delta-1,\Delta,q+\Delta-1,q+\Delta$ and every source and
relation determinant in OSP30.

\subsection{The resulting same-source moment target}

The moments in OSP27 are completely specified by the original
analytic identity OSP9:
\[
\mu_j^{(s)}=\int y^j\,dm_s(y)
=M_s\left.\frac{d^j}{dz^j}(\cos z)^{-s/2}\right|_{z=0},
\qquad
\mathcal D_a(Q;s)=
\det[\mu_{2Q+i+j}^{(s)}]_{0\le i,j<a}.
\tag{OSP34}
\]
The differentiated integral is justified by OSP7, or directly by
the finite exponential moments on a slightly larger interval.
Odd moments vanish because the density is even. Reordering rows
and columns together by parity therefore proves the exact further
factorization
\[
\mathcal D_a(Q;s)
=\det[\mu_{2(Q+i+j)}^{(s)}]_{0\le i,j<\lceil a/2\rceil}
 \det[\mu_{2(Q+1+i+j)}^{(s)}]_{0\le i,j<\lfloor a/2\rfloor}.
\tag{OSP35}
\]
There is no permutation sign, since the same permutation is applied
to both rows and columns. Empty factors are one.
In OSP32 the coefficient of $\log M_s$ is
$\Delta+(\Delta+1)-(q+\Delta)-(q+\Delta+1)-1+q+(q+1)=0$.
This is an exact cancellation only after all original moments
and determinant dimensions have been retained.

Equation OSP33 proves an error-controlled comparison with the exact
finite determinant difference OSP32. It does not obtain a first
variation by differentiating a leading $q^2$ law. In particular no
numerical value of the limit of $\mathcal F_{0,k}^{(s)}/(kq)$ is
asserted by this comparison.

\section{The outer-root and actual residual bounds in the original arithmetic return}
\label{sec:OAR}
Retain the complete original data of CEP, CTV and ROQ. In particular
$m=1$, $k=4l+1\ge9$, $q=(k+1)^2$, $q'=(k-7)^2$,
$\Delta=16k-48$, $r=8k-16$ and $j=8k-32$. The quartet, full
amplitude unit, period and branch are the specified original ones on
the proved five-orbit locus. The source orders remain $s\in\{1,k\}$.
Every matrix below is the actual matrix in those chapters, with its
original mass and coefficient frame.

\subsection{The two finite error endpoints retain their signs}
Write
\[
 \mathcal N_+=\{q-1,q\},\qquad
 \mathcal N_-=\{2q-1,2q\},\qquad
 \epsilon_{A,k}^{(s)}=2\sum_{N\in\mathcal N_+\cup\mathcal N_-}E_N^{(s)}.
 \tag{OAR1}
\]
Here $E_N^{(s)}$ is the explicit full conductor constant of CEP35.
The nonnegative constants $L_N^{\rm tail},U_N^{\rm tail}$ are
exactly CTV18 in the same source order and with the original
$q'$, $\delta$, $\gamma$. Define
\[
 \begin{split}
 a_{k,s}^-&=v\left(\sum_{N\in\mathcal N_+}L_N^{\rm tail}
                         +\sum_{N\in\mathcal N_-}U_N^{\rm tail}\right),\\
 a_{k,s}^+&=v\left(\sum_{N\in\mathcal N_+}U_N^{\rm tail}
                         +\sum_{N\in\mathcal N_-}L_N^{\rm tail}\right),\\
 e_{k,s}^-&=\epsilon_{A,k}^{(s)}+a_{k,s}^-,\qquad
 e_{k,s}^+=\epsilon_{A,k}^{(s)}+a_{k,s}^+.
 \end{split}\tag{OAR2}
\]
These are finite quantities for every original period in the stated
domain. For each fixed original period, both $e_{k,s}^\pm=o(kq)$.
Indeed CEP36 proves this for $\epsilon_{A,k}^{(s)}$ and CTV18--20
proves it for each of the four tail contributions, uniformly over
the possible indices $0\le v\le80$ and both original source orders.
When $v=0$, both $a_{k,s}^\pm$ are exactly zero.

Set $\Phi_{k,s}=F_{\Xi,k}^{(s)}$ and retain the full outer quotient
$\mathcal F_{\partial,k}^{(s)}$ of CTV11--13. The exact identity is
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 F_K^{(s)}=\mathcal F_{\partial,k}^{(s)}-\Phi_{k,s}+\mathfrak e_{k,s},\\
 \mathfrak e_{k,s}=\mathcal E_{A,k}^{(s)}
     +\sum_{N\in\mathcal N_+}\mathcal R_{N,v}^{(s)}
     -\sum_{N\in\mathcal N_-}\mathcal R_{N,v}^{(s)},\\
 -e_{k,s}^-\le\mathfrak e_{k,s}\le e_{k,s}^+.
 \end{gathered}\tag{OAR3}
\]
The equality is CTV22, keeping its original two errors. CTV19 says
$-vL_N^{\rm tail}\le\mathcal R_{N,v}^{(s)}\le vU_N^{\rm tail}$.
At a positive endpoint this contributes lower bound $-vL_N^{\rm tail}$
and upper bound $vU_N^{\rm tail}$; at a negative endpoint it
contributes lower bound $-vU_N^{\rm tail}$ and upper bound
$vL_N^{\rm tail}$. Adding these four inequalities and the bounds
$-\epsilon_{A,k}^{(s)}\le\mathcal E_{A,k}^{(s)}
\le\epsilon_{A,k}^{(s)}$ proves each sign of OAR3.

\subsection{Original positive increments give explicit kernel caps}
The full value of $\Phi_{k,s}$ is ROQ19's finite sum
\[
 \Phi_{k,s}=\log(1+\eta_{q-1})
       +2\sum_{N=q}^{2q-2}\log(1+\eta_N)
       +\log(1+\eta_{2q-1}),\qquad
 \lambda_s=\log(1+\eta_{q-1})\ge0.
 \tag{OAR4}
\]
Every $\eta_N$ here is ROQ17's original constrained column, including
the complete conductor--observation cross covariance and its
positive denominator. No new observation is selected.
ROQ21 gives, in the original AKS notation,
\[
 \lambda_s\le\Phi_{k,s}\le
 V_s:=j(\mathcal L_{s,q}+\mathcal L_{s,q+1})-\lambda_s.
 \tag{OAR5}
\]
Retain the complete earlier kernel interval $L_s\le F_K^{(s)}\le U_s$
of AKJ2/MRI4e, with its pointwise minimum of the KAF and AKS bounds.
Define two explicit quantities
\[
 \begin{split}
 L_s^{\partial}&=\max\left\{L_s,
       \mathcal F_{\partial,k}^{(s)}-e_{k,s}^--V_s\right\},\\
 U_s^{\partial}&=\min\left\{U_s,
       \mathcal F_{\partial,k}^{(s)}+e_{k,s}^+-\lambda_s\right\}.
 \end{split}\tag{OAR6}
\]
Then
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 L_s^{\partial}\le F_K^{(s)}\le U_s^{\partial},\\
 \mathcal F_{\partial,k}^{(s)}-\Phi_{k,s}-e_{k,s}^-
       \le F_K^{(s)}
       \le\mathcal F_{\partial,k}^{(s)}-\Phi_{k,s}+e_{k,s}^+.
 \end{gathered}\tag{OAR7}
\]
For the first line substitute both ends of OAR5 into OAR3 and
intersect with the retained interval. The second line substitutes
the full finite value OAR4 into OAR3. Intersecting these intervals
preserves every bound. Both contain the actual value, so their
intersection is nonempty. The dimension $j$ is used only in the
proved finite comparison OAR5. It assigns no leading determinant.
Each additional evaluated positive term of OAR4 can be included
in the upper subtraction in OAR6 by the same inequality.

\subsection{The correlated arithmetic kernel and boundary}
Keep the original arithmetic total $\mathcal B_k^{\rm ar}$,
the scalar $\delta_k^\sigma$ and the four source-difference constants
$C_K^\pm,C_B^\pm$ of MRI4f. They satisfy, for the actual
$d=F_K^{\rm ar}-F_K^{(1)}$,
\[
 \max\{-C_K^-,\delta_k^\sigma-C_B^+\}\le d
       \le\min\{C_K^+,\delta_k^\sigma+C_B^-\}.
 \tag{OAR8}
\]
This is the pair of original kernel bounds together with the
boundary bounds, transferred by
$d+(F_B^{\rm ar}-F_B^{(1)})=\delta_k^\sigma$.
It retains their common scalar and signs. Define
\[
 \begin{split}
 L_{\rm ar}^{\partial}
   &=\max\{L_{\rm ar},L_1^{\partial}-C_K^-,
                    L_1^{\partial}+\delta_k^\sigma-C_B^+\},\\
 U_{\rm ar}^{\partial}
   &=\min\{U_{\rm ar},U_1^{\partial}+C_K^+,
                    U_1^{\partial}+\delta_k^\sigma+C_B^-\}.
 \end{split}\tag{OAR9}
\]
Here $[L_{\rm ar},U_{\rm ar}]$ is the complete interval of MRI4f.
Adding OAR8 to the source-$1$ first line of OAR7 proves
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 L_{\rm ar}^{\partial}\le F_K^{\rm ar}\le U_{\rm ar}^{\partial},\\
 \mathcal B_k^{\rm ar}-U_{\rm ar}^{\partial}
       \le F_B^{\rm ar}
       \le\mathcal B_k^{\rm ar}-L_{\rm ar}^{\partial}.
 \end{gathered}\tag{OAR10}
\]
The second line subtracts the first from the exact original identity
$F_K^{\rm ar}+F_B^{\rm ar}=\mathcal B_k^{\rm ar}$.
It uses the same arithmetic total at both endpoints. If the second
line of OAR7 is used instead, exactly the same addition and
subtraction yield the further interval containing the full residual
sum. Thus every exact positive residual subtraction is available to
the original arithmetic kernel and its correlated boundary.

\subsection{The signed mixed return with its complete finite error}
Write
$\mathfrak S_k^{\rm mix}=F_K^{\rm ar}+F_B^{\rm ar}-F_B^{(k)}$.
The original BRI6d identity is
$\mathfrak S_k^{\rm mix}=F_K^{(k)}+\mathcal H_k+\delta_k^\sigma$.
Consequently OAR3 gives the exact current expression
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \mathfrak S_k^{\rm mix}=\mathcal F_{\partial,k}^{(k)}-\Phi_{k,k}
              +\mathcal H_k+\delta_k^\sigma+\mathfrak e_{k,k},\\
 -e_{k,k}^-\le\mathfrak e_{k,k}\le e_{k,k}^+,
 \qquad e_{k,k}^\pm=o(kq).
 \end{gathered}\tag{OAR11}
\]
This substitution proves every sign, keeping the original Gamma
return and arithmetic scalar. Addition of their unchanged values
to the source-$k$ bounds OAR7 yields the corresponding finite
intervals for this same signed quantity. The full original
four-endpoint metrics, outer-root polynomial, weighted source,
period-dependent certificates and graph denominator remain in
OAR11 through their proved maps CTV and ROQ. The next leading-scale
calculation is the difference of these two explicit quotient returns.

\section{The same-source Gamma moment comparison in the arithmetic return}
\label{sec:PMR}
Retain every original parameter, matrix and error in OAR1--11.
The complete OSP comparison supplies an additional bound directly
on the actual outer-root quotient. Set $\epsilon=2^{-32}$ and
retain its explicit range
\[
 k\ge29,\qquad k\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2}
           \le\epsilon(k+1)^2/2.
 \tag{PMR1}
\]
This range contains all sufficiently large original $k=4l+1$ for
each fixed original quartet: $k\ge\max\{29,
2\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2}/\epsilon\}$ is sufficient because
$(k+1)^2\ge k^2$. For the remaining finite values the full earlier
OAR estimates remain valid without using this comparison.

Keep OSP24's nonnegative $\mathcal E_k$ and put
\[
 c_k^\circ=4(q+\Delta+1)\mathcal E_k,
 \qquad e_{k,s}^{0,-}=e_{k,s}^-+c_k^\circ,
 \qquad e_{k,s}^{0,+}=e_{k,s}^++c_k^\circ.
 \tag{PMR2}
\]
OSP26 and OSP33 prove $c_k^\circ=O_{\delta,\gamma}(q)=o(kq)$
on PMR1, uniformly for the unchanged source orders $s=1,k$.
The actual outer quotient differs from OSP32's exact seven
original Gamma moment determinants by at most $c_k^\circ$.
Consequently the full identity and signed bounds are
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 F_K^{(s)}=\mathcal F_{0,k}^{(s)}-\Phi_{k,s}+\mathfrak e^0_{k,s},\\
 \mathfrak e^0_{k,s}=\mathfrak e_{k,s}
       +\mathcal F_{\partial,k}^{(s)}-\mathcal F_{0,k}^{(s)},\\
 -e_{k,s}^{0,-}\le\mathfrak e^0_{k,s}\le e_{k,s}^{0,+},
 \qquad e_{k,s}^{0,\pm}=o(kq).
 \end{gathered}\tag{PMR3}
\]
The first two equalities are OAR3 with the displayed exact
difference added and subtracted. The two bounds follow by adding
the interval $[-c_k^\circ,c_k^\circ]$ of OSP33 to the unequal
OAR3 endpoints. No metric equality is substituted for the
proved OSP coefficient maps and determinant comparison.
The residual sum $\Phi_{k,s}$ retains all actual period data.

Let $V_s$ and $\lambda_s$ be OAR4--5's exact residual upper
bound and first positive increment. Define
\[
 \begin{split}
 L_s^0&=\max\{L_s^\partial,
                \mathcal F_{0,k}^{(s)}-e_{k,s}^{0,-}-V_s\},\\
 U_s^0&=\min\{U_s^\partial,
                \mathcal F_{0,k}^{(s)}+e_{k,s}^{0,+}-\lambda_s\}.
 \end{split}\tag{PMR4}
\]
Then $L_s^0\le F_K^{(s)}\le U_s^0$. To prove this, insert
$\lambda_s\le\Phi_{k,s}\le V_s$ into PMR3 and intersect
with OAR7. Using the full finite sum for $\Phi_{k,s}$ in PMR3
gives the sharper interval centred at
$\mathcal F_{0,k}^{(s)}-\Phi_{k,s}$. Both retain the same
unequal finite errors of PMR2.

The exact arithmetic correlations of OAR8 give
\[
 \begin{split}
 L_{\rm ar}^0&=\max\{L_{\rm ar}^\partial,L_1^0-C_K^-,
                                      L_1^0+\delta_k^\sigma-C_B^+\},\\
 U_{\rm ar}^0&=\min\{U_{\rm ar}^\partial,U_1^0+C_K^+,
                                      U_1^0+\delta_k^\sigma+C_B^-\}.
 \end{split}\tag{PMR5}
\]
Adding those correlations to PMR4 at $s=1$ proves
$L_{\rm ar}^0\le F_K^{\rm ar}\le U_{\rm ar}^0$.
Subtracting from the exact same arithmetic total gives
\[
 \mathcal B_k^{\rm ar}-U_{\rm ar}^0
      \le F_B^{\rm ar}\le\mathcal B_k^{\rm ar}-L_{\rm ar}^0.
 \tag{PMR6}
\]
Thus the actual kernel and boundary retain their common scalar
and both original source comparisons.

Finally the original signed-return identity BRI6d and PMR3 at
source order $k$ give
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 F_K^{\rm ar}+F_B^{\rm ar}-F_B^{(k)}
   =\mathcal F_{0,k}^{(k)}-\Phi_{k,k}
      +\mathcal H_k+\delta_k^\sigma+\mathfrak e^0_{k,k},\\
 -e_{k,k}^{0,-}\le\mathfrak e^0_{k,k}\le e_{k,k}^{0,+}.
 \end{gathered}\tag{PMR7}
\]
This follows by substituting into
$F_K^{\rm ar}+F_B^{\rm ar}-F_B^{(k)}=F_K^{(k)}+
\mathcal H_k+\delta_k^\sigma$; every sign is retained.
The entire original same-source moment expression is OSP32--35.
The next asymptotic calculation must evaluate it with the actual
residual sum and an error small compared with $kq$.

\paragraph{The exact finite endpoints under this comparison.}
The interval transport in PMR4--6 preserves the already retained
outer-root endpoints exactly:
\[
 L_s^0=L_s^\partial,\qquad U_s^0=U_s^\partial,\qquad
 L_{\rm ar}^0=L_{\rm ar}^\partial,\qquad
 U_{\rm ar}^0=U_{\rm ar}^\partial.
 \tag{PMR8}
\]
For proof, OSP33 gives
$\mathcal F_{0,k}^{(s)}-c_k^\circ\le\mathcal F_{\partial,k}^{(s)}
\le\mathcal F_{0,k}^{(s)}+c_k^\circ$.
The new lower candidate in PMR4 is therefore at most
$\mathcal F_{\partial,k}^{(s)}-e_{k,s}^--V_s$, which is at
most $L_s^\partial$ by OAR6. The new upper candidate is at
least $\mathcal F_{\partial,k}^{(s)}+e_{k,s}^+-\lambda_s$,
which is at least $U_s^\partial$. Taking the displayed maximum
and minimum proves the source equalities. Substitution in PMR5
and the defining maxima and minima OAR9 proves the arithmetic
equalities; subtracting from the same total proves equality of
the boundary endpoints as well. Thus this comparison supplies
the exact same-source moment target and controlled error; a
further numerical improvement must use sharper evaluated moment
or residual information. The preceding ROQ/OAR bounds remain
the proved finite intervals throughout this transport.

# Complete independent proof review: CTV1–22

Reviewer: `/root/mixed_row_morphism_review`.
Date: 2026-09-15.
Source: `../ORIGINAL_TOTAL_VARIATION_CHRISTOFFEL.tex`.
Accepted source SHA-256: `0efc3faba03dad4a1f42be0f9ab6808b0903aa57fc3f2c7a032e869be40f10cb`.
Disposition: **ACCEPTED. No outstanding mathematical defects.**

Every definition, formula, and proof in CTV1–22 was independently read. The final changes were reread: the moment determinant is defined for nonzero polynomial `P`, the exponential-moment reference is CTV14, and the positive moment constant is consistently named `mathfrak c_mom=8/pi`. No local base-symbol reuse remains. This review concerns the complete mathematical proof; it does not claim the author's separate exact fixtures, a PDF rendering, or a publication.

## Original coordinate maps and nested polynomials, CTV1–5

The source order is exactly `s=1` or `s=k` for both grids. The full source mass, Gamma density, and monic norms are unchanged. The four signs and primary frames in CTV2 match CEP49.

Pulling back the monic characteristic polynomial along `S=c+iy` multiplies its highest-degree term by `i^q`; thus the displayed factor `i^(-q)` makes precisely the monic polynomial in `y`. The lower grid has its own factor `i^(-q')`. Both factors and both original centres are explicitly retained.

For each lower index, `2(a+4)-k=2a-(k-8)` and the same identity holds in the second coordinate. Therefore `omega'_(a,b)=omega_(a+4,b+4)` exactly. The central rectangle has `(k-7)^2=q'` entries. The complementary set has `Delta=q-q'=16k-48` entries. Both products are monic, so CTV4 is an exact factorization with no unspecified scalar.

Since the lower grid degree is odd, every `|2a-k'|>=1`. A real `y` is at distance at least the modulus of the imaginary part of each lower root, which is at least `delta`. Multiplying every factor proves CTV5. The root-radius bound `R'=k' sqrt(delta^2+gamma^2)` follows from the two original coordinate bounds. These facts use the actual roots and do not require any period coefficient lower bound.

## Full determinant factors and orientations, CTV6–9

With nonzero `P`, the moment matrices in CTV6 are positive definite: for a nonzero coefficient vector, the corresponding polynomial times `P` is nonzero and has only finitely many real zeros; its squared modulus integrates positively against the positive original measure. The exponential moment proved in CTV14 ensures every required moment is finite. The empty determinant convention is consistent.

For CTV7 the increasing-degree frame consists of the monomial remainder columns followed by the columns `P,yP,...`. Monicity gives a triangular coordinate change with determinant one. Its lower-right Gram block is the full relation moment determinant, and its Schur complement is the actual minimum quotient metric. The determinant orientation is therefore full source divided by relation, exactly as displayed. Monic orthogonalization of the original Gamma source also has determinant one, giving the product of all `h_n` in the numerator. The empty-relation endpoint retains that full numerator.

The affine original-coordinate change in degree below the quotient dimension has diagonal entries `i^j` and determinant of modulus one. The relation columns acquire their original `i^q` or `i^q'` factor together with the corresponding triangular change of their multiplying monomials, all of determinant modulus one. Evaluating polynomial coefficient classes in the primary basis multiplies vectors by the original Vandermonde. Thus the primary metric is the inverse-congruence metric and its determinant is divided by the squared modulus of that Vandermonde determinant. This proves the orientations in CTV8.

At the lower source cutoff `d=N-v`, the relation dimension is

`d-q'+1=N-v-q'+1=t+Delta-v`.

Taking the quotient of the two CTV8 identities leaves exactly the `v` high source norms `h_(N-v+1),...,h_N`, plus the lower relation logarithm and minus the upper relation logarithm. The two nonzero Vandermonde factors are independent of `N`; their signed coefficient is `1+1-1-1=0`. This proves CTV9 and retains all four relation determinants.

## Exact weighted-source quotient and every shifted index, CTV10–13

Multiplication by the full lower polynomial is injective and satisfies the exact norm equality

`||P_lower f||_(m_s)^2=integral |f|^2 |P_lower|^2 dm_s`.

This proves CTV10's source map including the full mass and its specified image in the original degree cutoff. It does not introduce a new Gamma order.

At source degree `L=N-q'=t+Delta-1`, the quotient by the outer polynomial has remainder dimension `Delta`. Its relation columns are `P_outer y^j`, `0<=j<t`. In the weighted measure their complete Gram is `D_t(P_k;s)` by the exact nested factorization. Their full source Gram is `D_(t+Delta)(P_lower;s)`. Applying the same monic Schur calculation proves CTV12 with the displayed numerator and denominator.

The positive weighted moment matrices define the monic orthogonal polynomial by minimum projection onto lower powers. Its squared norm is the Schur complement, so

`lambda_j=D_(j+1)(P_lower;s)/D_j(P_lower;s)`.

The ratio `D_(t+Delta-v)/D_(t+Delta)` is therefore the inverse product of the `v` consecutive norms indexed from `t+Delta-v` through `t+Delta-1`. Since `t+Delta-1=N-q'`, these are exactly the indices `N-q'-a`, `0<=a<v`. The retained source-norm indices are `N-a`. This proves every sign and index of the tail in CTV13.

The four outer-source degrees are `Delta-1,Delta,q+Delta-1,q+Delta`, with signs `+,+,-,-`. Their quotient frame is the same original monomial remainder frame at each endpoint. For the smallest possible norm index, `N-q'-(v-1)>=Delta-v>=16`; hence none of the logarithms uses a negative index. At `v=0` the tail is empty and the exact equality remains valid.

## Full weighted monic-norm estimates, CTV14–19

The original density and its complete mass give the Laplace transform `M_s (cos t)^(-b)` on `|t|<pi/2`. Its scaling is consistent with the original monic norms: in particular its second moment is `M_s b=h_1`. Evenness makes the Laplace integral equal to the integral of `cosh(t y)`. Each nonnegative Taylor term bounds its own even moment. At `t_0=pi/4`, taking the square root and using `(2j)!<=4^j(j!)^2` gives exactly the CTV14 monomial norm bound with `mathfrak c_mom=2/t_0=8/pi`. The complete mass and order remain in that bound.

For a monic degree-`n` polynomial with every root of modulus at most `R'`, each degree-`a` coefficient is a sum of `binom(n,a)` root products of degree `n-a`. Its absolute value is therefore bounded by `binom(n,a)(R')^(n-a)`. Multiplying this by the monomial norm bound, summing all coefficients, and setting `h=n-a` gives

`sqrt(M_s)(cos t_0)^(-b/2) mathfrak c_mom^n n! sum_(h=0)^n (R'/mathfrak c_mom)^h/h!`.

Increasing this nonnegative finite sum to the exponential series proves CTV15 without omitting any coefficient contribution.

For the upper bound on `lambda_j`, the monic competitor `y^j` produces the actual product `P_lower y^j`, whose degree is `q'+j` and whose extra roots are exactly zero. It satisfies the same root-radius bound, so CTV15 gives the displayed upper bound in CTV16. For the lower bound, CTV5 applies pointwise to every competing monic polynomial. Its original Gamma norm is at least the exact monic minimum `h_j`. Taking the minimum therefore yields `delta^(2q') h_j`. This proves both bounds with the original measure.

For `n=N-a`, `j=n-q'`, subtracting the logarithm of the upper norm bound from `log h_n` gives the lower expression in CTV17:

`b log(cos t_0)+log((b)_n/n!)-2n log mathfrak c_mom-2R'/mathfrak c_mom`.

Subtracting the lower norm bound gives its upper expression:

`sum_(r=j+1)^n (log r+log(b+r-1))-2q' log delta`.

The two full `log M_s` contributions cancel only in this exact same-source comparison. No mass was discarded from either individual norm.

The elementary weight-ratio estimate of CEP19 yields `|log((b)_n/n!)|<=c_b^log H_n`. The original endpoint indices give `n<=N`, while `log(8/pi)>0`. The lower CTV17 expression is therefore at least `-L_N^tail`. In the upper expression there are exactly `n-j=q'` terms, each bounded by `log N+log(b+N-1)`; since `0<delta<1/2`, the remaining term is `2q'|log delta|`. This proves the upper bound `U_N^tail`. Every term defining these constants is nonnegative on the displayed original domain. Summing the `v` terms proves both one-sided bounds and their maximum in CTV19, including its exact zero case.

## Uniform tail scale, explicit metric, and combined return, CTV20–22

For either original source, `b<=k/2`, while `c_b^log=O(k)`, `N<=2q`, `q'<=q`, and `R'<=k sqrt(delta^2+gamma^2)`. The explicit lower-tail constant is therefore `O_(delta,gamma)(q+k log(q+1))`; the upper-tail constant is `O_delta(q log(q+1))`. Multiplication by any `0<=v<=80` preserves the stated uniform bound. Division by `kq` tends to zero because `q=(k+1)^2` and `log(q+1)/k` tends to zero. This proves CTV20 without a bound on an unevaluated period coefficient and without differentiating a prior asymptotic.

The literal remainder matrix in CTV21 is onto since its first `Delta` columns are the identity. The stated lift is its exact minimum source lift: direct multiplication yields the input, and the residual lift lies in the orthogonal relation kernel. Thus its inverse covariance is the same actual quotient metric used in CTV11–12, in the same monomial frame.

Finally CEP49 gives `F_K=T_total-F_Xi+E_A`, while CTV13 gives `T_total=F_outer+sum sigma R_tail`. Substitution proves every sign of CTV22. The triangle inequality gives exactly

`|F_K-F_outer+F_Xi| <= 2 sum_N E_N + sum_N C_(N,v)^tail = o(kq)`.

The first error retains its fixed-actual-period scope. The new tail estimate is uniform over all possible moment indices and does not depend on the remaining period coordinates. The outer quotient has actual rank `16k-48`, and the original observation quotient has rank `8k-32`; both retain their specified source metrics and endpoint maps. No value or existence of a limit for their remaining leading difference is asserted by this reduction.

## Final disposition

The full proof is accepted on the pinned source. The explicit nonzero-polynomial hypothesis resolves the only literal generality defect identified during review. The corrected citation and moment-symbol rename are also verified. No accepted RUI/CEP source, sealed 110-page reader, or previous delivery was edited in this review lane.

# Complete independent proof review: ROQ1–27

Reviewer: `/root/mixed_row_morphism_review`.
Date: 2026-09-15.
Source: `../ORIGINAL_RESIDUAL_OBSERVATION_QUOTIENT.tex`.
Accepted SHA-256: `20fbdae33e8387d880b8ac9c1c7b6433512fb077ae21922d0a43fd5fd1080966`.
Disposition: **ACCEPTED. No outstanding mathematical defects.**

Every definition, formula, and full proof in ROQ1–27 was independently read. The reviewer also read complete RCA1–22 and rechecked the original AKS7–10/15–16 and OCF2–7/17/24–26 providers. These include the original Segre orientation, coefficient elimination, fourteen-generator recursion, exact word Gram, and actual observation duality. The source's repaired `\quad` and denominator-span wording were present in the inspected final file. This report does not certify a new PDF, formal run, fixture execution, or publication.

## Original dual coefficient maps and observation, ROQ1–8

The primary roots, original period matrix, unit, branch, and complete conductor coefficients are retained. The conductor matrix has the original stencil, and its ordinary transpose multiplies biform coefficients in the original lexicographic order. No conjugation belongs to this bilinear coefficient map.

OCF's finite elimination gives exactly `S N+C^T V=I` and `N S=I`, with `ker N=im C^T`. Transposition therefore gives `I_V=N^T` as the precise map from strip dual coordinates to `ker C`, with inverse `S^T` restricted to that kernel. In particular, for `Cx=0`, the transposed first identity gives `x=N^T S^T x`. This verifies ROQ2–3, including both inverse identities.

2. A small nested polynomial fixture P_lower=(y-3)^2+1/16,
   P_outer=(y+3)^2+1/16 verifies the general determinant identities
   independently using literal remainder matrices and minimum Gram
   inverses. Its degrees 4,2 are diagnostic and are not the k=9/13
   programme dimensions. Both original Gamma orders 1 and 9 are

from pathlib import Path
from functools import lru_cache
import hashlib
import json
import sys
import sympy as sp

OUT = Path(sys.argv[1])
y = sp.Symbol("y")
I = sp.I
delta, gamma = sp.Rational(1,4), sp.Integer(3)


def require(condition, label):
    if not condition:
        raise RuntimeError(label)


def same(A, B, label):
    require(A.shape == B.shape and all(sp.cancel(z)==0 for z in A-B), label)


def inv(A):
    return A.applyfunc(sp.expand).inv(method="DM")


def determinant(A):
    return sp.cancel(A.det(method="domain-ge"))


def grid_check(k):
    kp=k-8
    omega={(a,b):(2*b-k)*gamma-I*(2*a-k)*delta
           for a in range(k+1) for b in range(k+1)}
    lower={(a,b):(2*b-kp)*gamma-I*(2*a-kp)*delta
           for a in range(kp+1) for b in range(kp+1)}
    require(all(omega[(a+4,b+4)]==value for (a,b),value in lower.items()),
            "exact original central-index equality")
    outer=[z for (a,b),z in omega.items() if not(4<=a<=k-4 and 4<=b<=k-4)]
    require(len(set(omega.values()))==(k+1)**2,"upper roots distinct")
    require(len(outer)==(k+1)**2-(k-7)**2,"outer degree")
    require(set(omega.values())==set(lower.values())|set(outer)
            and set(lower.values()).isdisjoint(outer),"exact monic root factor")
    require(all(abs(sp.im(z))>=delta for z in lower.values()),
            "every lower root has retained imaginary distance")
    return {"k":k,"q":len(omega),"q_prime":len(lower),"outer_degree":len(outer),
            "status":"PASS"}

endpoints=(q-1,q,2*q-1,2*q)
signs=(1,1,-1,-1)


def moment_sequence(b,count):
    # y*p_j=p_(j+1)+j*(b+j-1)*p_(j-1), with the original monic
    # recurrence. The p_0 coefficient is the integral divided by M.
    state=[sp.Integer(0)]*(count+2)
    state[0]=sp.Integer(1)
    moments=[state[0]]
    for step in range(count):
        nxt=[sp.Integer(0)]*(count+2)
        for j in range(step+1):
            nxt[j+1]+=state[j]
            if j:
                nxt[j-1]+=state[j]*j*(b+j-1)

        moments.append(sp.cancel(state[0]))

    def weighted_moment(key,n):

                             for a in range(squared.degree()+1)))

                          for a in range(L+1)])

    def D(key,size):
        return sp.Integer(1) if not size else determinant(H(key,size-1))
    def R(P,L):
        return sp.Matrix([[sp.rem(sp.Poly(y**n,y),P).nth(a) for n in range(L+1)]
                          for a in range(P.degree())])
    def minimum_gram(P,L,key):
        r=R(P,L)
        return inv(r*inv(H(key,L))*r.T)

    Qproduct=sp.Integer(1)
    tails=sp.Integer(1)

No numerical value is assigned to delta, gamma, or an actual period.
The lattice test uses k=9, the first literal endpoint family of CTV.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from fractions import Fraction
from hashlib import sha256
from math import comb
from pathlib import Path
import json
import sys
import time

import sympy as sp
from sympy.polys.rings import ring
from sympy.polys.domains import ZZ

sys.set_int_max_str_digits(0)
HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
started = time.time()
report = {"parameter_values": "delta and gamma remain indeterminates",
          "period_values": "none assigned", "checks": []}

k = 9
kp = k - 8
q, qp = (k + 1)**2, (kp + 1)**2
Delta = q - qp
assert (q, qp, Delta) == (100, 4, 96)
upper = {(2*b-k, 2*a-k) for a in range(k+1) for b in range(k+1)}
central = {(2*(b+4)-k, 2*(a+4)-k)
           for a in range(kp+1) for b in range(kp+1)}
lower = {(2*b-kp, 2*a-kp) for a in range(kp+1) for b in range(kp+1)}
assert central == lower and lower < upper
assert {(-u, -v) for u, v in upper} == upper
assert len(upper-lower) == Delta
report["checks"].append({"name": "literal root-lattice nesting and symmetry",
                         "k": k, "q": q, "q_prime": qp, "Delta": Delta})

# Y=y^2, d=delta^2, g=gamma^2. Each factor retains a complete quartet
# of the actual grid: roots +/-v*gamma +/-i*u*delta.
R, Y, d, g = ring("Y,d,g", ZZ)
def quartet(u, v):
    return Y**2 + 2*(u*u*d-v*v*g)*Y + (u*u*d+v*v*g)**2

P = R.one
Pcentral = R.one
Pouter = R.one
for u in range(1, k+1, 2):
    for v in range(1, k+1, 2):
        factor = quartet(u, v)
        P *= factor
        if u <= kp and v <= kp:
            Pcentral *= factor
        else:
            Pouter *= factor
assert Pcentral * Pouter == P
assert P.degree(Y)*2 == q
assert Pcentral.degree(Y)*2 == qp
assert Pouter.degree(Y)*2 == Delta
assert P[(q//2, 0, 0)] == 1 and Pouter[(Delta//2, 0, 0)] == 1
for exponents in P:
    assert sum(exponents) == q//2
report["checks"].append({"name": "complete symbolic original polynomial factorization",
                         "coefficient_ring": "Z[y^2,delta^2,gamma^2]",
                         "full_terms": len(P), "outer_terms": len(Pouter),
                         "full_coefficient_sha256":

# Check the literal monic division morphism, including all 96 target directions.
y, ds, gs = sp.symbols("y delta_squared gamma_squared")
outer_expr = sum(int(c)*y**(2*ey)*ds**ed*gs**eg
                 for (ey, ed, eg), c in Pouter.items())
divisor = sp.Poly(outer_expr, y, domain=sp.ZZ[ds, gs])
L = Delta + 2
for j in range(L+1):
    image = sp.Poly(y**j, y, domain=divisor.domain) if j < Delta else divisor.mul(
        sp.Poly(y**(j-Delta), y, domain=divisor.domain))
    assert image.degree() == j and image.LC() == 1
    quotient, remainder = image.div(divisor)
    if j < Delta:
        assert quotient.is_zero and remainder == image
    else:
        assert remainder.is_zero
        assert quotient == sp.Poly(y**(j-Delta), y, domain=divisor.domain)
report["checks"].append({"name": "literal quotient intertwiner and determinant-one frame",
                         "rank": Delta, "source_degree": L,
                         "all_columns_checked": L+1})

def scaled_original_moments(b, maximum):
    # f(z)=(cos z)^(-b), cos(z) f'(z)=-b cos'(z) f(z).
    # M_n=f^(n)(0); recurrence retains the full original source parameter b.
    values = [Fraction(0) for _ in range(maximum+1)]
    values[0] = Fraction(1)
    for n in range(2, maximum+1, 2):
        total = Fraction(0)
        for j in range(2, n+1, 2):
            total += ((1-b)*j-n)*comb(n,j)*((-1)**(j//2))*values[n-j]
        values[n] = total/n
    answer = []
    for n, value in enumerate(values):
        scaled = value*(2**n)
        assert scaled.denominator == 1
        answer.append(int(scaled))
    return answer

def det_bareiss(rows):
    A = [row[:] for row in rows]
    n = len(A)
    if n == 0:
        return 1
    previous = 1
    for pivot_index in range(n-1):
        pivot = A[pivot_index][pivot_index]
        assert pivot > 0  # All matrices here are positive Gram matrices.
        for i in range(pivot_index+1, n):
            left = A[i][pivot_index]
            for j in range(pivot_index+1, n):
                numerator = A[i][j]*pivot-left*A[pivot_index][j]
                quotient, remainder = divmod(numerator, previous)
                assert remainder == 0
                A[i][j] = quotient
            A[i][pivot_index] = 0
        previous = pivot
    return A[-1][-1]

# This is an actual low endpoint dimension and lower-grid power.
# The scalar normalization is explicit:
# det A = 2^(2*Q*a+a*(a-1)) * D_a(Q;s) / M_s^a.

    assert determinant > 0 and determinant == determinant_even*determinant_odd

        "determinant_bit_length": determinant.bit_length(),
        "determinant_sha256": sha256(str(determinant).encode()).hexdigest(),
        "identity": "det(full)=det(even)*det(odd)"})
    print(f"Exact parity determinant passed for s={s}, a={a}, Q={Q}.", flush=True)

% Exact original-primary covariance of V_A/K; independent calculation.
\section{The original residual observation covariance and its endpoint increments}
\label{sec:RCA}

Retain the original simple-quartet data, source order, source mass,
ordered primary coordinates, conductor coefficients and conductor matrix
of CEP1--4. In particular
\[
 k=4l+1\ge9,\quad q=(k+1)^2,\quad q'=(k-7)^2,\quad
 \Delta=q-q',\quad r=8k-16,\quad t=\Delta-r=8k-32.
 \tag{RCA1}
\]
The source order is the fixed choice $s\in\{1,k\}$ throughout
every cutoff calculation. Write $b=s/2$, $M_s=(2\pi)^{s/2}$ and
$h_n=M_s n!(b)_n$. At all cutoffs $N\ge q-1$ let
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 (U_N)_{(i,j),n}=
  \frac{p_n((\beta_{ij}-k/2)/\mathrm i)}{\sqrt{h_n}},
 \qquad 0\le n\le N,\\
 R_N=U_NU_N^*>0,\qquad G_N=R_N^{-1},\qquad
 A_N^C=CR_NC^*>0 .
 \end{gathered}\tag{RCA2}
\]
Here $\mathrm i^2=-1$, and $p_n$, $\beta_{ij}$ and the positive
square root of $h_n$ are exactly those of CEP21. The star denotes
conjugate transpose. The superscript on $A_N^C$ avoids confusion
with the rectangular source conductor $A_N$ in CEP14.
The first $q$ columns of $U_N$ have a nonzero evaluation
Vandermonde determinant, and $C$ has full row rank $q'$ by CEP4.
These facts prove both strict inequalities in RCA2.

\subsection{The exact residual covariance in the original coordinates}

Fix the original coefficient frame
$I_V:\mathbb C^\Delta\hookrightarrow E_k$ of $V_A=\ker C$.
Let $\Xi:\mathbb C^\Delta\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb C^t$
be the actual observation map from CEP27, with $I_V\ker\Xi=K$.
A concrete extension to the original primary coordinates is
\[
 J_V=(I_V^*I_V)^{-1}I_V^*,\qquad
 D=\Xi J_V:\mathbb C^q\longrightarrow\mathbb C^t,
 \qquad DI_V=\Xi .
 \tag{RCA3}
\]
The positive matrix $I_V^*I_V$ is invertible because $I_V$
is injective. This left inverse specifies a coordinate map;
the metric used below remains the original $G_N$.
Any explicit original observation rows having restriction $\Xi$
to $I_V\mathbb C^\Delta$ can be used as $D$ instead, with the
same formulas and values proved below. Define
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 H_{V,N}=I_V^*G_NI_V,\\
 W_N=R_N-R_NC^*(A_N^C)^{-1}CR_N,\\
 \Omega_N=DW_ND^*,\qquad Q_N=\Omega_N^{-1}.
 \end{gathered}\tag{RCA4}
\]
All inverses displayed in RCA4 exist. The exact identities are
\[
 W_N=I_V H_{V,N}^{-1}I_V^*,\qquad
 \Omega_N=\Xi H_{V,N}^{-1}\Xi^*>0,\qquad Q_N=Q_{\Xi,N}.
 \tag{RCA5}
\]
To prove them put $B_C=CR_N^{1/2}$. Then $B_CB_C^*=A_N^C>0$,
and multiplication verifies that
$P_C=I-B_C^*(B_CB_C^*)^{-1}B_C$ is a Hermitian
idempotent with range $\ker B_C$. Thus
$W_N=R_N^{1/2}P_CR_N^{1/2}$ is positive semidefinite,
has rank $\Delta$, and has range $\ker C$.
It has the form $I_V T I_V^*$ with $T>0$:
take $T=J_VW_NJ_V^*$ and use that $I_VJ_V$ is the identity
on the range of $W_N$. Multiplication using $CI_V=0$
gives $W_NG_NI_V=I_V$. Consequently
$I_VT H_{V,N}=I_V$, hence $T=H_{V,N}^{-1}$.
Since $DI_V=\Xi$, the second formula follows; its strict
positivity follows from the full row rank of $\Xi$.
The last formula is the specified quotient of CEP27.

For every $y\in\mathbb C^t$ its actual minimum-norm lift
in $V_A$ and its squared norm are
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 x_N(y)=W_ND^*Q_Ny,\quad Cx_N(y)=0,\quad Dx_N(y)=y,\\
 x_N(y)^*G_Nx_N(y)=y^*Q_Ny .
 \end{gathered}\tag{RCA6}
\]
Indeed its coordinate lift is $z=H_{V,N}^{-1}\Xi^*Q_Ny$.
Every other coordinate lift differs by $a\in\ker\Xi$,
and $a^*H_{V,N}z=a^*\Xi^*Q_Ny=0$. Pythagoras proves
the minimum and uniqueness, and substitution proves its norm.

The stacked original-coordinate map
\[
 B=\begin{pmatrix}C\\D\end{pmatrix}:
 E_k\longrightarrow\mathbb C^{q'}\oplus\mathbb C^t
 \tag{RCA7}
\]
is surjective and has kernel $K$. First lift a prescribed
$C$-coordinate using the surjectivity of $C$, then correct its
$D$-coordinate by a member of $V_A$, using the surjectivity of
$D|_{V_A}$. This proves surjectivity, and its kernel is exactly
$I_V\ker\Xi=K$. Its covariance has the full block form
\[
 BR_NB^*=
 \begin{pmatrix}A_N^C&CR_ND^*\\DR_NC^*&DR_ND^*\end{pmatrix}>0,
 \qquad
 \det(BR_NB^*)=\det(A_N^C)\det\Omega_N .
 \tag{RCA8}
\]
Subtracting $DR_NC^*(A_N^C)^{-1}$ times the first block row
from the second has determinant one and gives second diagonal
block $\Omega_N$, proving the identity. In particular
\[
 \log\det Q_N=\log\det A_N^C-\log\det(BR_NB^*).
 \tag{RCA9}
\]
The mixed block $CR_ND^*$ is retained in this exact formula.

Every extension $D'$ with the same restriction to $V_A$ has
$D'=D+LC$: choose a right section $L_C$ of $C$ and put
$L=(D'-D)L_C$; then $x-L_CCx\in\ker C$ proves the assertion.
Since $CW_N=W_NC^*=0$, this change preserves $\Omega_N$.
More generally an invertible coordinate change $T$ of $\Xi$
has the exact rules
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 D'=TD+LC,\quad \Omega_N'=T\Omega_NT^*,\quad
 Q_N'=T^{-*}Q_NT^{-1},\\
 \log\det Q_N'=\log\det Q_N-2\log|\det T|.
 \end{gathered}\tag{RCA10}
\]
These follow by multiplication. The constant term cancels at
the four endpoints only after applying $1,1,-1,-1$.

\subsection{The next original source column, with every cross term retained}

For $n\ge q$, retain the exact next source column
\[
 (u_n)_{(i,j)}=
 \frac{p_n((\beta_{ij}-k/2)/\mathrm i)}
      {\sqrt{M_s n!(s/2)_n}},
 \qquad R_n=R_{n-1}+u_nu_n^* .
 \tag{RCA11}
\]
An omitted cutoff in the following calculation denotes $n-1$.
Define
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 c_n=Cu_n,\quad d_n=Du_n,\quad
 a_n=1+c_n^*(A^C)^{-1}c_n>0,\\
 w_n=u_n-RC^*(A^C)^{-1}c_n\in V_A,\qquad
 \eta_n=Dw_n=d_n-DRC^*(A^C)^{-1}c_n .
 \end{gathered}\tag{RCA12}
\]
Then the exact updates are
\[
 W_n=W_{n-1}+\frac{w_nw_n^*}{a_n},\qquad
 \Omega_n=\Omega_{n-1}+\frac{\eta_n\eta_n^*}{a_n}.
 \tag{RCA13}
\]
To verify every cross term put $v=RC^*(A^C)^{-1}c_n$,
$z=c_n^*(A^C)^{-1}c_n$ and $u=u_n$ only in this calculation.
Multiplication verifies
\[
 (A^C+c_nc_n^*)^{-1}
 =(A^C)^{-1}
 -\frac{(A^C)^{-1}c_nc_n^*(A^C)^{-1}}{1+z}.
 \tag{RCA14}
\]
Since $(R+uu^*)C^*=RC^*+uc_n^*$, expansion gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 &(RC^*+uc_n^*)(A^C+c_nc_n^*)^{-1}(CR+c_nu^*)\\
 &=RC^*(A^C)^{-1}CR+vu^*+uv^*+z uu^*
       -\frac{(v+zu)(v+zu)^*}{1+z}.
 \end{split}
\]
Subtracting from $R+uu^*$, the coefficients of $uu^*$,
$vu^*$, $uv^*$ and $vv^*$ in $W_n-W_{n-1}$ are respectively
$1/(1+z)$, $-1/(1+z)$, $-1/(1+z)$ and $1/(1+z)$.
This gives the first formula in RCA13; multiplication by
$D,D^*$ gives the second. Also
$Cw_n=c_n-A^C(A^C)^{-1}c_n=0$.

Apply the verified inverse identity RCA14 to $\Omega_n$:
\[
 Q_n=Q_{n-1}-
 \frac{Q_{n-1}\eta_n\eta_n^*Q_{n-1}}
      {a_n+\eta_n^*Q_{n-1}\eta_n}.
 \tag{RCA15}
\]
The denominator is positive, proving $Q_n\le Q_{n-1}$ as
quadratic forms in the same original quotient coordinates.
The exact scalar determinant change is
\[
 \ell_{\Xi,n}:=\log\det Q_{n-1}-\log\det Q_n
 =\log\left(1+\frac{\eta_n^*Q_{n-1}\eta_n}{a_n}\right)\ge0.
 \tag{RCA16}
\]
For a direct determinant proof, conjugate $\Omega_n$ by
$\Omega_{n-1}^{-1/2}$. The matrix becomes $I+zz^*$ with
$z=\Omega_{n-1}^{-1/2}\eta_n/\sqrt{a_n}$.
It acts as the identity on $z^\perp$ and as multiplication
by $1+z^*z$ on the span of $z$. The case $z=0$ is the
identity. Taking determinants and then inverting proves RCA16.

\subsection{The exact positive return and its complementary shares}

The remaining original observation return of CEP49 is
\[
 \begin{split}
 F_{\Xi,k}^{(s)}
 &=\ell_{\Xi,q}+2\sum_{n=q+1}^{2q-1}\ell_{\Xi,n}
                       +\ell_{\Xi,2q}\ge0,\\
 \ell_{\Xi,n}
 &=\log\left(1+
 \frac{\eta_n^*Q_{n-1}\eta_n}
 {1+(Cu_n)^*(CR_{n-1}C^*)^{-1}Cu_n}\right).
 \end{split}\tag{RCA17}
\]
Indeed $\log\det Q_{q-1}-\log\det Q_{2q-1}$ telescopes
RCA16 from $q$ through $2q-1$; and
$\log\det Q_q-\log\det Q_{2q}$ telescopes it from $q+1$
through $2q$. Their sum has exactly these weights.
Equality holds if and only if $\eta_n=0$ at every
$q\le n\le2q$, since all weights are positive and $Q_{n-1}>0$.
No monotonicity of the separate increments is needed.

There is a further exact identity describing how the original
restrictions and quotient share every increment. Define
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 h_{E,n}=u_n^*R_{n-1}^{-1}u_n,\\
 h_{C,n}=(Cu_n)^*(CR_{n-1}C^*)^{-1}Cu_n,\\
 h_{B,n}=(Bu_n)^*(BR_{n-1}B^*)^{-1}Bu_n .
 \end{gathered}\tag{RCA18}
\]
These real numbers satisfy $0\le h_{C,n}\le h_{B,n}\le h_{E,n}$.
To prove this put $z=R_{n-1}^{-1/2}u_n$.
For either full-row-rank map $J=C,B$, the matrix
\[
 P_J=R_{n-1}^{1/2}J^*(JR_{n-1}J^*)^{-1}JR_{n-1}^{1/2}
\]
is the orthogonal projection onto
$\operatorname{im}(R_{n-1}^{1/2}J^*)$, by multiplication.
The range for $C$ is contained in the range for $B$,
because the rows of $C$ are the first rows of $B$.
The squared norms of these two projections of $z$ are
$h_{C,n},h_{B,n}$, while $z^*z=h_{E,n}$.
Orthogonal decomposition proves all inequalities.

The inverse block form of RCA8 gives
\[
 h_{B,n}=h_{C,n}+\eta_n^*Q_{n-1}\eta_n,\qquad
 \ell_{\Xi,n}=\log\frac{1+h_{B,n}}{1+h_{C,n}}.
 \tag{RCA19}
\]
Here is an explicit proof of the inverse form used:
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}A&E\\E^*&F\end{pmatrix}
 =\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\E^*A^{-1}&I\end{pmatrix}
  \begin{pmatrix}A&0\\0&F-E^*A^{-1}E\end{pmatrix}
  \begin{pmatrix}I&A^{-1}E\\0&I\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Multiplying the right side proves the equality.
Its inverse quadratic form on $(Cu_n,Du_n)$ uses
$A=CR_{n-1}C^*$ and $E=CR_{n-1}D^*$.
The second transformed coordinate is exactly $\eta_n$,
and the second diagonal inverse is $Q_{n-1}$.
This proves the first identity in RCA19; RCA16 proves the second.

For the fixed original frame $I_K$ of $K$ put
$H_{K,N}=I_K^*G_NI_K$. The two restriction determinant drops are
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \ell_{V,n}:=\log\det H_{V,n-1}-\log\det H_{V,n}
             =\log\frac{1+h_{E,n}}{1+h_{C,n}},\\
 \ell_{K,n}:=\log\det H_{K,n-1}-\log\det H_{K,n}
             =\log\frac{1+h_{E,n}}{1+h_{B,n}},\\
 \ell_{V,n}=\ell_{K,n}+\ell_{\Xi,n},\qquad
 \ell_{K,n},\ell_{\Xi,n}\ge0 .
 \end{gathered}\tag{RCA20}
\]
For a direct proof for each restriction, let $J$ be either
$C$ or $B$ with kernel frame $I$. The original metric update,
verified as in RCA14, is $G_n=G-Guu^*G/(1+u^*Gu)$.
Thus $I^*G_nI=H-aa^*/(1+h_E)$, where $H=I^*GI$ and
$a=I^*Gu$. RCA5's proof for the full-row-rank $J$ gives
$I H^{-1}I^*=R-RJ^*(JRJ^*)^{-1}JR$. Multiplication yields
$a^*H^{-1}a=h_E-h_J$.
Conjugating the metric update by $H^{-1/2}$, its determinant
ratio is $1-(h_E-h_J)/(1+h_E)=(1+h_J)/(1+h_E)>0$.
This follows by the same one-dimensional eigenvalue argument
as RCA16. Taking negative logarithms proves the first two
formulas; subtraction and RCA18 prove the remaining assertions.

Write $\mathcal L(f)=f_q+2\sum_{n=q+1}^{2q-1}f_n+f_{2q}$.
Applying these identical positive weights to RCA20 proves
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 F_{V_A}^{(s)}=\mathcal L(\ell_V),\qquad
 F_K^{(s)}=\mathcal L(\ell_K),\qquad
 F_{\Xi,k}^{(s)}=\mathcal L(\ell_\Xi),\\
 0\le F_{\Xi,k}^{(s)}\le F_{V_A}^{(s)},\qquad
 0\le F_K^{(s)}\le F_{V_A}^{(s)},\qquad
 F_{V_A}^{(s)}=F_K^{(s)}+F_{\Xi,k}^{(s)}.
 \end{gathered}\tag{RCA21}
\]
This proves the exact decomposition at every column increment,
in addition to the four-endpoint frame cancellation of CEP27.

Finally set $\epsilon_k^{(s)}=2\sum_N E_N$ with the exact
four cutoffs and constants of CEP35. Combining CEP49 with
RCA21 gives the finite inequalities
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 0\le F_K^{(s)}\le\mathcal T_k^{(s)}+\epsilon_k^{(s)},\qquad
 0\le F_{\Xi,k}^{(s)}\le\mathcal T_k^{(s)}+\epsilon_k^{(s)},\\
 \mathcal T_k^{(s)}\ge-\epsilon_k^{(s)},\qquad
 \epsilon_k^{(s)}=o(kq)
 \quad\hbox{for the fixed actual quartet and period.}
 \end{gathered}\tag{RCA22}
\]
The sharper finite identity remains
$F_K^{(s)}=\mathcal T_k^{(s)}-F_{\Xi,k}^{(s)}
+\mathcal E_{A,k}^{(s)}$ of CEP49, now with every term
of $F_{\Xi,k}^{(s)}$ evaluated by RCA12 and RCA17.
No leading coefficient for this sum is assigned here.
RCA17 gives the exact positive terms with full original
cross covariances that can be estimated at the actual periods.
